sys_remote_update_set.description: ServiceNow Case Management POC scoped application : proof-of-concept replatforming of a subset of ArkCase case/task/party/role/portal/dashboard capabilities. AAP Section 0.4.1 single Update Set deliverable.
sys_remote_update_set.name: x_casemgmt_case_management v1.0.0

sys_update_xml.name: Case Management
sys_update_xml.payload: <record_update table="sys_app"> <sys_app action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"> <active>true</active> <description>Proof-of-concept ServiceNow scoped application that re-platforms a defined subset of ArkCase 2021.03 case-management capabilities onto the ServiceNow Now Platform. Implements seven enumerated POC capabilities: (1) the case lifecycle as the x_casemgmt_case table replicating ArkCase CaseFile fields; (2) the task domain as x_casemgmt_case_task replicating ArkCase AcmTask fields; (3) polymorphic party association as a single x_casemgmt_case_party table that collapses ArkCase PersonAssociation and PersonOrganizationAssociation; (4) three scoped roles (case_manager, case_agent, case_viewer) with table-level and field-level ACLs replacing ArkCase ApplicationRolesToPrivilegesConfig; (5) two Flow Designer flows (one per case type: General Inquiry, Complaint) replacing the Activiti BPMN state machine; (6) an Experience Portal with two unauthenticated pages (case submission and case status lookup); and (7) two Performance Analytics dashboards (Agent Workspace and Manager View). All artifacts live in the auto-assigned x_casemgmt namespace; zero global-scope writes are made. No external integrations, no email notifications, no document management, and no data migration from ArkCase are performed.</description> <enforce_license>false</enforce_license> <licensable>false</licensable> <logo /> <name>x_casemgmt Case Management</name> <private>false</private> <scope>x_casemgmt</scope> <source>x_casemgmt</source> <short_description>Proof-of-concept ServiceNow re-platforming of ArkCase case-management capabilities.</short_description> <sys_id>82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_id> <trackable>true</trackable> <vendor>ServiceNow Case Management POC</vendor> <vendor_prefix>x_casemgmt</vendor_prefix> <version>1.0.0</version> </sys_app> </record_update>

sys_update_xml.payload: <record_update table="sys_dictionary"> <sys_dictionary action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"> <active>true</active> <array>false</array> <attributes/> <audit>false</audit> <calculation/> <choice>0</choice> <choice_field/> <choice_table/> <column_label>Opened Date</column_label> <comments>DateTime auto-set on case creation via ../business_rules/x_casemgmt_set_opened_date.xml. The single most important field on the x_casemgmt_case_party table - it ties every party row (Person or Organization) back to its parent case. Replaces ArkCase PersonAssociation.parentId/parentType/parentTitle polymorphic parent linkage (and the equivalent on PersonOrganizationAssociation); in this POC the parent is always a x_casemgmt_case row, so the polymorphism is collapsed into a single fixed-target reference. Powers the case-form Related List rendering (AAP Section 0.4.4) so that case parties show under the case form. Used by case_agent "Assigned only" ACL conditions on x_casemgmt_case_party via dot-walk current.case.assigned_agent / current.case.assigned_group (AAP Section 0.5.6). Cascade rule is "none" - deleting a parent case does NOT auto-cascade-delete its child parties (POC-safe default; manual cleanup required). Seed data resolves the parent-case sys_id by lookup of x_casemgmt_case.number via ../scripts/seed_demo_data.js (no hardcoded sys_ids, per AAP Section 0.7.2).</comments> <create_roles/> Conditional: required when party_type=Person (enforced by UI Policy in ../ui_policy/x_casemgmt_case_party_conditional_fields.xml). Replaces ArkCase PersonAssociation.person and PersonOrganizationAssociation.person @ManyToOne (which targeted ArkCase's Person entity; here we leverage OOB sys_user instead). Person half of the polymorphism collapse pattern (AAP Section 0.4.3): when party_type=Person this field is required and visible while the sibling organization field is hidden; when party_type=Organization this field is hidden while organization is required. Cascade rule is empty (default "no cascade" - deleting a sys_user does NOT auto-cascade-delete party rows; manual cleanup of orphaned references is acceptable). Conditional: required when party_type=Organization (enforced by UI Policy in ../ui_policy/x_casemgmt_case_party_conditional_fields.xml). Replaces ArkCase PersonOrganizationAssociation.organization @ManyToOne (which targeted ArkCase's Organization entity; here we leverage OOB core_company instead). sys_update_xml.name: x_casemgmt_case_read_agent_assigned
sys_update_xml.payload:
<record_update table="sys_security_acl">
    <sys_security_acl action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE">
        <active>true</active>
        <admin_overrides>true</admin_overrides>
        <advanced>true</advanced>
        <condition/>
        <description>Table-level ACL: x_casemgmt_case_agent can read x_casemgmt_case records ONLY when assigned_agent = current user OR assigned_group contains current user (per AAP Section 0.5.6 'Assigned only'). Affects list views, form load, related lists, report rows, and dashboard aggregates - any unauthorized case row is filtered out of every read surface.</description>
        <name>x_casemgmt_case</name>
        <operation>read</operation>
        <roles>x_casemgmt_case_agent</roles>
        <script><![CDATA[(function() {
    var currentUserId = gs.getUserID();
    if (current.assigned_agent == currentUserId) {
        return true;
    }
    if (current.assigned_group && !current.assigned_group.nil()) {
        var groupId = current.assigned_group.toString();
        if (groupId && gs.getUser().isMemberOf(groupId)) {
            return true;
        }
    }
    return false;
})();]]></script>
        <sys_class_name>sys_security_acl</sys_class_name>
        <sys_created_by>admin</sys_created_by>
        <sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on>
        <sys_id>ed26b2ef9256d55de66e4c1ac7b1997e</sys_id>
        <sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count>
        <sys_name>x_casemgmt_case</sys_name>
        <sys_package display_value="Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">x_casemgmt</sys_package>
        <sys_policy/>
        <sys_scope display_value="Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope>
        <sys_update_name>sys_security_acl_x_casemgmt_case_read_agent_assigned</sys_update_name>
        <sys_updated_by>admin</sys_updated_by>
        <sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on>
        <type>record</type>
    </sys_security_acl>
</record_update>

        <description>Field-level ACL: x_casemgmt_case_manager can always write assigned_agent; x_casemgmt_case_agent can write assigned_agent only if they are the currently-assigned agent on the case. Allows agent self-reassignment without permitting case-grabbing.</description>
        <name>x_casemgmt_case.assigned_agent</name>
        <operation>write</operation>
        <roles>x_casemgmt_case_manager,x_casemgmt_case_agent</roles>
        <script><![CDATA[(function() {
    // Per AAP Section 0.5.1: "Field-level ACL: write restricted to
    // manager and agent-assigned". Per AAP Section 0.5.6 Matrix and
    // Section 0.7.3 Gate 3 ("case_agent cannot access unassigned
    // cases"), this script must DENY by default and grant only to
    // (a) any case_manager, and (b) the currently-assigned case_agent.

    // Branch 1: case_manager - unconditional grant.
    // The manager is the case-management tier's delegation authority;
    // they may freely assign, reassign, or null-out the assigned_agent
    // column on any case in the scoped application.
    if (gs.getUser().hasRole('x_casemgmt_case_manager')) {
        return true;
    }

    // Branch 2: currently-assigned case_agent - conditional grant.
    // The agent may modify assigned_agent (handoff, decline, reassign
    // to peer) ONLY when they are the currently-assigned agent on the
    // case at write time. The strict equality check against
    // gs.getUserID() prevents:
    //   - non-assigned agents from self-grabbing unassigned cases
    //     (current.assigned_agent is null - comparison yields false)
    //   - non-assigned agents from poaching other agents' cases
    //     (current.assigned_agent is a peer's sys_id - comparison
    //      yields false)
    //   - non-agent role holders from being granted via this branch
    //     (the hasRole() guard filters them out before the comparison)
    // The comparison `current.assigned_agent == gs.getUserID()` works
    // in ServiceNow because GlideRecord reference fields auto-resolve
    // to their sys_id when compared as strings; this is the standard
    // pattern used throughout the platform's ACL conditions.
    if (gs.getUser().hasRole('x_casemgmt_case_agent')) {
        if (current.assigned_agent == gs.getUserID()) {
            return true;
        }
    }

    // Default: deny. Viewers, anonymous users, and any other role
    // populations fall through to this branch. Per AAP Section 0.5.6
    // case_viewer has Write=No on every column of x_casemgmt_case;
    // this default-deny implements that mandate at the field level.
    return false;
})();]]></script>
        <sys_class_name>sys_security_acl</sys_class_name>
        <sys_created_by>admin</sys_created_by>
        <sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on>
        <sys_id>3719a93101a32c5e06c9907fbcfa8d03</sys_id>
        <sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count>
        <sys_name>x_casemgmt_case.assigned_agent</sys_name>
        <sys_package display_value="Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">x_casemgmt</sys_package>
        <sys_policy/>
        <sys_scope display_value="Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope>
        <sys_update_name>sys_security_acl_x_casemgmt_case_assigned_agent_field_acl</sys_update_name>
        <sys_updated_by>admin</sys_updated_by>
        <sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on>
        <type>record</type>
    </sys_security_acl>
</record_update>

sys_update_xml.name: CaseTransitionValidator
sys_update_xml.payload:
<record_update table="sys_script_include">
    <sys_script_include action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE">
        <access>package_private</access>
        <active>true</active>
        <api_name>x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator</api_name>
        <caller_access/>
        <client_callable>false</client_callable>
        <description>Central transition-guard helper for the case state-machine. Provides canTransitionToOpen/canTransitionToInProgress/canTransitionToResolved/canTransitionToClosed, validateNoBacktransition, isAgentInGroup, and getOpenTaskCountForCase. Called by all Flow Designer flows, Business Rules, and UI Actions in the x_casemgmt scope. ServiceNow-native equivalent of ArkCase ChangeCaseFileStateService. All transition rules and verbatim error messages are traced to AAP Section 0.5.5 and 0.7.4. canTransitionToResolved blocks the In Progress -> Resolved transition with the verbatim message "All tasks must be closed before resolving this case." when any child x_casemgmt_case_task has status != Closed. validateNoBacktransition blocks any -> Draft with the verbatim message "Cases cannot be returned to Draft." and Closed -> * with the verbatim message "Closed cases are terminal and cannot be modified." Role checks use gs.getUser().hasRole(role_name) only. Group-membership checks use GlideRecord on sys_user_grmember (read-only). Open-task counting uses GlideAggregate on x_casemgmt_case_task. Contains zero hardcoded sys_id literals in references and zero gs.eventQueue() calls per the email-disabled constraint.</description>
        <name>CaseTransitionValidator</name>
        <script><![CDATA[var CaseTransitionValidator = Class.create();
CaseTransitionValidator.prototype = {
    /**
     * No-arg initializer. The class holds no per-instance state across
     * calls (each guard call from a flow/Business Rule/UI Action is
     * stateless), so initialize() is intentionally empty. Keeping the
     * empty initializer lets callers use the platform-canonical
     * `new x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator()` instantiation pattern.
     */
    initialize: function() {
    },

    /**
     * Validates the Draft -> Open transition.
     *
     * Per AAP Section 0.5.5 (verbatim):
     *     | From  | To   | Required condition         | Failure handling          |
     *     | Draft | Open | assigned_group populated   | Surface form-level error  |
     *
     * The caller (the validate_open_transition.xml subflow or a
     * before-update Business Rule) surfaces the returned {error} string
     * via gs.addErrorMessage() + current.setAbortAction(true) so the
     * blocking-error message appears on the form per AAP Section 0.7.1
     * ("Surface all blocking errors on the form").
     *
     * @param {GlideRecord} caseGr - the case record being transitioned
     *     (typically the platform-injected `current` GlideRecord in a
     *     before-update Business Rule, or the case record loaded by the
     *     Flow Designer subflow).
     * @return {Object} { ok: true } when valid, or
     *     { ok: false, error: 'Required field assigned_group is empty.' }
     *     when assigned_group is null/empty/whitespace, or
     *     { ok: false, error: 'Case record is missing.' } when caseGr
     *     is null/undefined.
     */
    canTransitionToOpen: function(caseGr) {
        if (!caseGr) {
            return { ok: false, error: 'Case record is missing.' };
        }
        // GlideRecord.getValue() returns the column's string value or
        // null. Coerce to String defensively (some platform releases
        // return GlideElement objects instead of primitives) and trim
        // whitespace. An assigned_group that is a single space character
        // is functionally empty for the purposes of this guard.
        var assignedGroup = caseGr.getValue('assigned_group');
        if (!assignedGroup || String(assignedGroup).trim() === '') {
            return { ok: false, error: 'Required field assigned_group is empty.' };
        }
        return { ok: true };
    },

    /**
     * Validates the Open -> In Progress transition.
     *
     * Per AAP Section 0.5.5 (verbatim):
     *     | From | To          | Required condition                                      | Failure handling          |
     *     | Open | In Progress | assigned_agent populated AND member of assigned_group   | Surface form-level error  |
     *
     * Both conditions are checked. If assigned_agent is unset, OR
     * assigned_group is unset, OR the assigned_agent is set but is not a
     * member of the assigned_group (verified by isAgentInGroup), the
     * transition is blocked. The single error message is intentionally
     * uniform across all three failure modes so a probing client cannot
     * distinguish which precondition failed (defense against
     * privilege-escalation reconnaissance).
     *
     * @param {GlideRecord} caseGr - the case record being transitioned.
     * @return {Object} { ok: true } when valid, or
     *     { ok: false, error: 'Assigned agent must be set and must be a member of the assigned group.' }
     *     when any precondition fails, or
     *     { ok: false, error: 'Case record is missing.' } when caseGr
     *     is null/undefined.
     */
    canTransitionToInProgress: function(caseGr) {
        if (!caseGr) {
            return { ok: false, error: 'Case record is missing.' };
        }
        // Same defensive String() coercion + trim() as canTransitionToOpen.
        var assignedAgent = caseGr.getValue('assigned_agent');
        var assignedGroup = caseGr.getValue('assigned_group');
        if (!assignedAgent || String(assignedAgent).trim() === '') {
            return { ok: false, error: 'Assigned agent must be set and must be a member of the assigned group.' };
        }
        if (!assignedGroup || String(assignedGroup).trim() === '') {
            return { ok: false, error: 'Assigned agent must be set and must be a member of the assigned group.' };
        }
        // Membership check delegated to isAgentInGroup. The sys_ids
        // passed in are RUNTIME values (read from the case record), NOT
        // hardcoded literals - this complies with AAP Section 0.7.2's
        // no-hardcoded-sys_id constraint.
        if (!this.isAgentInGroup(String(assignedAgent), String(assignedGroup))) {
            return { ok: false, error: 'Assigned agent must be set and must be a member of the assigned group.' };
        }
        return { ok: true };
    },

    /**
     * Validates the In Progress -> Resolved transition.
     *
     * Per AAP Section 0.5.5 (verbatim):
     *     | From        | To       | Required condition                                  | Failure handling                                          |
     *     | In Progress | Resolved | All linked x_casemgmt_case_task have status=Closed | "All tasks must be closed before resolving this case."    |
     *
     * Per AAP Section 0.7.4 (verbatim error message):
     *     "All tasks must be closed before resolving this case."
     *
     * The string above MUST appear character-for-character in the return
     * value when at least one child task has status != 'Closed'. The
     * caller (validate_resolved_transition.xml subflow or a future
     * before-update Business Rule) passes this message to
     * gs.addErrorMessage(), which surfaces it on the form.
     *
     * Implementation delegates to getOpenTaskCountForCase, which uses
     * GlideAggregate for an efficient COUNT(*) query rather than
     * fetching task rows. The boolean predicate (count > 0) is computed
     * here so the validator's API stays uniform.
     *
     * Semantic source-side reference: ArkCase
     * CaseFileTasksServiceImpl.java line 45-50
     * (acm-plugins/acm-default-plugins/acm-case-file-plugin/src/main/
     *  java/com/armedia/acm/plugins/casefile/service/
     *  CaseFileTasksServiceImpl.java) delegated to a Solr
     * ChildDocumentsSearchService for a comparable count; the
     * ServiceNow target uses the platform-native GlideAggregate
     * because Solr is out of POC scope per AAP Section 0.3.2.
     *
     * @param {GlideRecord} caseGr - the case record being transitioned.
     * @return {Object} { ok: true } when zero open child tasks remain,
     *     or { ok: false, error: 'All tasks must be closed before resolving this case.' }
     *     when at least one child task has status != Closed, or
     *     { ok: false, error: 'Case record is missing.' } when caseGr
     *     is null/undefined.
     */
    canTransitionToResolved: function(caseGr) {
        if (!caseGr) {
            return { ok: false, error: 'Case record is missing.' };
        }
        // GlideRecord.getUniqueValue() returns the sys_id of the current
        // row. This sys_id is a RUNTIME value (computed by the platform
        // when the case row was inserted), NOT a hardcoded literal.
        var openCount = this.getOpenTaskCountForCase(String(caseGr.getUniqueValue()));
        if (openCount > 0) {
            // VERBATIM AAP Section 0.7.4 error message - DO NOT paraphrase.
            return { ok: false, error: 'All tasks must be closed before resolving this case.' };
        }
        return { ok: true };
    },

    /**
     * Validates the Resolved -> Closed transition.
     *
     * Per AAP Section 0.5.5 (verbatim):
     *     | From     | To     | Required condition                                          | Failure handling          |
     *     | Resolved | Closed | Caller has x_casemgmt_case_manager role; auto-set closed_date | Surface form-level error  |
     *
     * The role check uses gs.getUser().hasRole(role_name) which accepts
     * the role's NAME ('x_casemgmt_case_manager') as a stable
     * human-readable key per AAP Section 0.7.2. This is the canonical
     * pattern for role checks in scoped applications - it does NOT
     * require a hardcoded role sys_id.
     *
     * The closed_date side-effect is NOT performed here. It is the
     * responsibility of two separate artifacts:
     *   - ../business_rules/x_casemgmt_set_closed_date.xml (catches
     *     direct DB updates: Table API, scripted REST, GlideRecord
     *     scripts, bulk imports)
     *   - ../flows/sub_flows/validate_closed_transition.xml (catches
     *     interactive transitions through the form/UI)
     * Defense in depth between these two writers is intentional;
     * see set_closed_date.xml's documentation for details.
     *
     * Dual-mode userId argument:
     *   - When userId is empty/null OR equals gs.getUserID() - use
     *     gs.getUser() (the current session user) - this is the
     *     standard interactive-form-update path.
     *   - When userId is non-empty AND differs from gs.getUserID() -
     *     look up the named user by sys_id, then call
     *     gs.getUser(user_name).hasRole(role_name) - this supports
     *     scheduled flows or system-context calls that validate
     *     transitions on behalf of a specific user (e.g., "did
     *     [requested user] have the case_manager role at request
     *     time?").
     *
     * @param {GlideRecord} caseGr - the case record being transitioned.
     * @param {String} userId - sys_id of the user attempting the
     *     transition. Typically gs.getUserID() (the current session
     *     user); may be a different sys_id for system-context calls.
     *     If null/empty, defaults to the current session user.
     * @return {Object} { ok: true } when the user has the case_manager
     *     role, or { ok: false, error: 'Only case managers can close cases.' }
     *     when the role check fails, or
     *     { ok: false, error: 'Case record is missing.' } when caseGr
     *     is null/undefined.
     */
    canTransitionToClosed: function(caseGr, userId) {
        if (!caseGr) {
            return { ok: false, error: 'Case record is missing.' };
        }
        // hasManagerRole resolves the case_manager role membership for
        // the user identified by userId. Three branches:
        //   (a) userId is provided and equals the current session user
        //       -> gs.getUser() is the most efficient path.
        //   (b) userId is provided and differs from the current user
        //       -> look up the named user by sys_id, then resolve
        //          their roles via gs.getUser(user_name).
        //   (c) userId is null/empty -> default to current session user.
        var hasManagerRole;
        if (userId && String(userId).trim() !== '' && String(userId) === String(gs.getUserID())) {
            hasManagerRole = gs.getUser().hasRole('x_casemgmt_case_manager');
        } else if (userId && String(userId).trim() !== '') {
            // Non-current-user context: look up the user record by the
            // RUNTIME sys_id passed in by the caller (NOT a hardcoded
            // literal). The user_name is the stable human-readable key
            // that gs.getUser() accepts; this satisfies the AAP Section
            // 0.7.2 stable-key constraint.
            var userGr = new GlideRecord('sys_user');
            if (userGr.get(String(userId))) {
                hasManagerRole = gs.getUser(String(userGr.getValue('user_name'))).hasRole('x_casemgmt_case_manager');
            } else {
                // Unknown user sys_id -> deny by default. Returning
                // false rather than throwing keeps the validator's
                // failure modes uniform (always {ok:false,error:string}).
                hasManagerRole = false;
            }
        } else {
            hasManagerRole = gs.getUser().hasRole('x_casemgmt_case_manager');
        }
        if (!hasManagerRole) {
            return { ok: false, error: 'Only case managers can close cases.' };
        }
        return { ok: true };
    },

    /**
     * Validates that a status change does not violate the prohibited
     * transitions enumerated in AAP Section 0.5.5.
     *
     * Two prohibited patterns - both with VERBATIM error messages
     * per AAP Section 0.7.4:
     *
     *   1. Closed -> anything (except staying Closed). Closed is the
     *      terminal state. The verbatim error message:
     *           "Closed cases are terminal and cannot be modified."
     *
     *   2. Any non-Draft state -> Draft. Backtransitioning to Draft is
     *      prohibited because Draft is reserved for new cases (the
     *      portal submission and dictionary default both produce Draft;
     *      no transition path returns to it). The verbatim error
     *      message:
     *           "Cases cannot be returned to Draft."
     *
     * The method is designed to be called from before-update Business
     * Rules where:
     *     previousStatus = String(previous.status)  // value BEFORE update
     *     newStatus      = String(current.status)   // proposed value
     * Flow Designer subflows can pass equivalent values via flow
     * variables.
     *
     * Edge cases handled gracefully:
     *   - Insert (previousStatus is null/empty): no transition to
     *     validate -> { ok: true }. This lets the same method be called
     *     from before-INSERT Business Rules (where previous is null)
     *     without producing false rejections.
     *   - newStatus is null/empty: no proposed value -> { ok: true }.
     *   - Closed -> Closed: not a real transition (no field change) ->
     *     { ok: true }.
     *   - Whitespace-only inputs: trimmed before comparison.
     *
     * @param {String} previousStatus - the previous status (e.g.,
     *     'Open', 'In Progress', 'Pending', 'Resolved', 'Closed', or
     *     '' on insert).
     * @param {String} newStatus - the new/proposed status. Must be one
     *     of the choice values in
     *     ../choices/sys_choice_case_status.xml.
     * @return {Object} { ok: true } when the proposed transition is
     *     allowed, or { ok: false, error: 'Closed cases are terminal and cannot be modified.' }
     *     when transitioning out of Closed, or
     *     { ok: false, error: 'Cases cannot be returned to Draft.' }
     *     when transitioning to Draft from any non-Draft state.
     */
    validateNoBacktransition: function(previousStatus, newStatus) {
        // Defensive coercion. The caller may pass GlideElement objects,
        // primitives, null, or undefined. String() of null/undefined
        // produces 'null' / 'undefined' which would otherwise compare
        // unexpectedly; the explicit ternary covers that case.
        var prev = previousStatus ? String(previousStatus).trim() : '';
        var next = newStatus ? String(newStatus).trim() : '';

        // Case 1: Closed is terminal - no transitions out.
        // The (next !== 'Closed' && next !== '') guard avoids false
        // rejections for:
        //   - Closed -> Closed (no field change; not a real transition)
        //   - Closed -> '' (proposed value is empty/cleared; not a
        //     real transition; the caller's other guards or dictionary
        //     mandatory flag will reject the empty value separately)
        if (prev === 'Closed' && next !== 'Closed' && next !== '') {
            // VERBATIM AAP Section 0.7.4 error message - DO NOT paraphrase.
            return { ok: false, error: 'Closed cases are terminal and cannot be modified.' };
        }

        // Case 2: Any non-Draft -> Draft is prohibited.
        // The (prev !== '' && prev !== 'Draft') guard avoids false
        // rejections for:
        //   - INSERT (prev is empty -> no transition to validate; the
        //     dictionary default value places new rows in Draft and
        //     this is the canonical entry point)
        //   - Draft -> Draft (no field change; harmless no-op)
        if (prev !== '' && prev !== 'Draft' && next === 'Draft') {
            // VERBATIM AAP Section 0.7.4 error message - DO NOT paraphrase.
            return { ok: false, error: 'Cases cannot be returned to Draft.' };
        }

        return { ok: true };
    },

    /**
     * Helper: returns true when the user is a member of the group.
     *
     * Implementation queries the OOB sys_user_grmember table, the
     * canonical group-membership join table in ServiceNow. Each
     * sys_user_grmember row links a `user` field (reference ->
     * sys_user) to a `group` field (reference -> sys_user_group); a
     * single matching row is sufficient evidence of membership.
     *
     * No hardcoded sys_ids: the userSysId and groupSysId arguments are
     * RUNTIME values supplied by the caller (typically read from the
     * case record's assigned_agent / assigned_group fields). This
     * helper never embeds a literal sys_id.
     *
     * setLimit(1) is a defensive optimization. At most one membership
     * row exists per (user, group) pair, but setting an explicit limit
     * tells the database engine to short-circuit at the first hit and
     * eliminates any potential for a misconfiguration to fetch all
     * membership rows of a populous group.
     *
     * Used by:
     *   - this.canTransitionToInProgress (Open -> In Progress validation)
     *   - ../business_rules/x_casemgmt_validate_assigned_agent_membership.xml
     *     (before-update guard on the case row that re-validates
     *     membership any time assigned_agent changes)
     *
     * @param {String} userSysId - sys_id of a sys_user record. May be
     *     null, undefined, empty, or whitespace-only - all of which
     *     are treated as "not a member" without throwing.
     * @param {String} groupSysId - sys_id of a sys_user_group record.
     *     Same null/empty handling as userSysId.
     * @return {Boolean} true if at least one sys_user_grmember row
     *     links the given user to the given group; false otherwise
     *     (including when either argument is null/empty).
     */
    isAgentInGroup: function(userSysId, groupSysId) {
        if (!userSysId || !groupSysId) {
            return false;
        }
        // Normalize whitespace-only strings to empty so the GlideRecord
        // query never receives a meaningless filter value.
        var userVal = String(userSysId).trim();
        var groupVal = String(groupSysId).trim();
        if (userVal === '' || groupVal === '') {
            return false;
        }
        var memberGr = new GlideRecord('sys_user_grmember');
        memberGr.addQuery('user', userVal);
        memberGr.addQuery('group', groupVal);
        memberGr.setLimit(1);
        memberGr.query();
        return memberGr.next() ? true : false;
    },

    /**
     * Helper: returns the count of OPEN child tasks for the given
     * case (i.e., child case_task rows where status != 'Closed').
     *
     * Implementation uses GlideAggregate, which executes a SQL
     * COUNT(*) directly in the database rather than fetching task
     * rows into the application layer. This is meaningfully more
     * efficient than GlideRecord.getRowCount() for cases with many
     * tasks, and is the correct pattern for count-only checks.
     *
     * No hardcoded sys_ids: the caseSysId argument is a RUNTIME value
     * supplied by the caller (typically caseGr.getUniqueValue()). This
     * helper never embeds a literal sys_id.
     *
     * The status filter uses the literal Title Case value 'Closed' -
     * this matches the choice list defined in
     * ../choices/sys_choice_case_task_status.xml (Open, In Progress,
     * Closed). ServiceNow Choice fields persist the LABEL string by
     * default, not an integer ID, so the != filter compares the
     * stored string value directly.
     *
     * Used by:
     *   - this.canTransitionToResolved (the In Progress -> Resolved
     *     gate; per AAP Section 0.5.5, the transition is allowed only
     *     when this method returns 0).
     *   - Diagnostic logging in calling flows (e.g., the
     *     validate_resolved_transition subflow may log the count
     *     when blocking the transition, although the user-facing
     *     error message is fixed verbatim per AAP Section 0.7.4).
     *
     * @param {String} caseSysId - sys_id of the parent
     *     x_casemgmt_case row. May be null, undefined, empty, or
     *     whitespace-only - all of which return 0 without throwing.
     * @return {Number} count of x_casemgmt_case_task rows where
     *     case = caseSysId AND status != 'Closed'. Returns 0 when
     *     caseSysId is invalid or no rows match.
     */
    getOpenTaskCountForCase: function(caseSysId) {
        if (!caseSysId || String(caseSysId).trim() === '') {
            return 0;
        }
        var caseVal = String(caseSysId).trim();
        // GlideAggregate constructor takes the table name. The scoped
        // table x_casemgmt_case_task is defined in
        // ../tables/x_casemgmt_case_task.xml and its `case` field is
        // the parent reference (defined in
        // ../dictionary/x_casemgmt_case_task_case.xml).
        var agg = new GlideAggregate('x_casemgmt_case_task');
        agg.addQuery('case', caseVal);
        // 'Closed' is the literal Title Case choice value from
        // ../choices/sys_choice_case_task_status.xml. The != operator
        // selects all OPEN tasks (Open, In Progress, and any future
        // non-Closed choice values added without breaking this guard).
        agg.addQuery('status', '!=', 'Closed');
        agg.addAggregate('COUNT');
        agg.query();
        if (agg.next()) {
            // getAggregate returns a string; parseInt with radix 10 is
            // the canonical numeric coercion. The defensive isNaN check
            // covers the unlikely case where the platform returns a
            // non-numeric string for an empty result set.
            var n = parseInt(agg.getAggregate('COUNT'), 10);
            return isNaN(n) ? 0 : n;
        }
        return 0;
    },

    /**
     * Class-name marker. ServiceNow's Class.create() pattern conventionally
     * exposes a `type` property whose value matches the class name
     * (without the scope prefix). This is used by the platform's
     * introspection tooling and by some debug logging. It MUST be
     * 'CaseTransitionValidator' (NOT 'x_casemgmt_CaseTransitionValidator')
     * - the scope prefix lives only in the <api_name> element above,
     * not in the class name itself.
     */
    type: 'CaseTransitionValidator'
};
]]></script>

sys_update_xml.name: CasePortalService
sys_update_xml.payload:
<record_update table="sys_script_include">
    <sys_script_include action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE">
        <access>package_private</access>
        <active>true</active>
        <api_name>x_casemgmt.CasePortalService</api_name>
        <caller_access/>
        <client_callable>false</client_callable>
        <description>Server-side helper for the unauthenticated Experience Portal. Provides submitCase(payload) for anonymous case submission and lookupCase(number) for anonymous status lookup. Enforces strict field whitelisting per AAP Section 0.7.4: submission accepts only subject, type, description, requester_name, requester_email and forces status=Draft regardless of payload; lookup returns only status, subject, opened_date and never exposes internal fields. submitCase returns {number} on success or {error} on failure; lookupCase returns the whitelisted record on match or null on no-match (the calling scripted REST endpoint translates null into the HTTP 404 not-found response whose verbatim body is specified by AAP Section 0.7.4). Replaces the persistence and lookup roles of ArkCase SaveCaseService and GetCaseByNumberService for the portal slice. Contains zero gs.eventQueue() calls per the email-disabled constraint and zero hardcoded sys_id reference literals.</description>
        <name>CasePortalService</name>
        <script><![CDATA[var CasePortalService = Class.create();
CasePortalService.prototype = {
    /**
     * No-arg initializer. The class holds no per-instance state across
     * calls (each request from the scripted REST handler instantiates a
     * fresh CasePortalService), so initialize() is intentionally empty.
     */
    initialize: function() {
    },

    /**
     * Anonymous case submission entry point.
     *
     * Whitelist-only field handling per AAP Section 0.7.4:
     *   - Accepted fields: subject, type, description, requester_name,
     *     requester_email
     *   - All other fields are silently dropped (no error returned for
     *     unrecognized keys; this matches the AAP requirement that the
     *     portal not surface internal field names to anonymous callers
     *     even by way of validation error messages).
     *   - status is FORCED to 'Draft' regardless of payload. Even if a
     *     malicious caller sends status='Closed' or any non-Draft value,
     *     the server overwrites to 'Draft' before insert. This is the
     *     single security guarantee that anonymous submissions cannot
     *     bypass the state-machine workflow.
     *   - Returns the auto-generated case number (CASE0000001 format)
     *     on success. The number generator is configured in
     *     ../numbers/sys_number_x_casemgmt_case.xml.
     *
     * Robust input handling per Rule 9 of the agent prompt: gracefully
     * handle null, undefined, and non-object payloads without throwing
     * uncaught exceptions (the unauthenticated REST endpoint can receive
     * any malformed payload from the public Internet).
     *
     * @param {Object} payload - request payload from the scripted REST
     *     endpoint, as parsed from the JSON request body.
     * @return {Object} { number: 'CASE0000001' } on success; or
     *     { error: '<message>' } on failure (invalid payload, insert
     *     rejected by validation business rule, post-insert lookup failed).
     */
    submitCase: function(payload) {
        // Defensive null/type check. The scripted REST endpoint should
        // already have parsed JSON into an object, but a malformed
        // request could yield null/undefined/string/array; guard against
        // all of those without leaking implementation details to the caller.
        if (!payload || typeof payload !== 'object' || Array.isArray(payload)) {
            return { error: 'Invalid payload.' };
        }

        var caseGr = new GlideRecord('x_casemgmt_case');
        caseGr.initialize();

        // Whitelisted input fields per AAP Section 0.7.4. The five fields
        // below are EXACTLY the inputs the case submission page exposes
        // to anonymous callers (../portal/pages/sp_page_x_casemgmt_case_submit.xml
        // and the submission widget at
        // ../portal/widgets/sp_widget_x_casemgmt_case_submission_widget.xml).
        // Any other key in the payload is silently dropped - we do not
        // even acknowledge unrecognized keys via an error response, so a
        // probing client cannot enumerate internal field names.
        var WHITELIST = ['subject', 'type', 'description', 'requester_name', 'requester_email'];
        for (var i = 0; i < WHITELIST.length; i++) {
            var fieldName = WHITELIST[i];
            // hasOwnProperty guards against prototype-pollution edge cases;
            // the != null check (loose equality) excludes both null AND
            // undefined while still allowing empty strings to pass through
            // (an empty-string requester_email is a valid "I do not wish
            // to provide email" answer that the dictionary marks optional).
            if (Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(payload, fieldName) && payload[fieldName] != null) {
                // String() coercion normalizes any non-string primitive
                // (number, boolean) into a string before the GlideRecord
                // setValue call - GlideRecord.setValue expects strings
                // for string-typed columns and the platform's behavior
                // for non-string inputs is release-dependent.
                caseGr.setValue(fieldName, String(payload[fieldName]));
            }
        }

        // FORCE status='Draft' regardless of payload (security perimeter).
        // Anonymous submissions ALWAYS start in Draft per AAP Sections
        // 0.5.5 and 0.7.4; the state-machine in the Flow Designer flows
        // (../flows/general_inquiry_state_machine.xml,
        // ../flows/complaint_state_machine.xml) advances the case from
        // Draft to subsequent statuses only via authenticated internal
        // user actions. Even if the dictionary's default_value='Draft'
        // already covers most insert paths, an explicit setValue() here
        // defends against a payload that includes status='Closed' (or
        // any other string) attempting to skip the state-machine entirely.
        caseGr.setValue('status', 'Draft');

        // Insert the new row. The insert() return value is the new
        // record's sys_id on success or null on failure. Failure here
        // typically indicates a before-insert business rule rejected the
        // record (e.g., a missing mandatory field that the portal client
        // forgot to send), or a database/platform error.
        var newSysId = caseGr.insert();
        if (!newSysId) {
            // gs.error() emits a diagnostic to the system log. Per Rule 5
            // of the agent prompt, we log getLastErrorMessage() (a
            // system-generated diagnostic) but NOT the raw payload (which
            // could carry PII like a real requester email). The error
            // returned to the caller is intentionally generic ("Submission
            // failed.") so a probing client cannot extract field-level
            // validation hints.
            gs.error('CasePortalService.submitCase: insert failed; lastErrorMessage=' + caseGr.getLastErrorMessage());
            return { error: 'Submission failed.' };
        }

        // Re-query by sys_id to read the auto-generated 'number' field.
        // The number is populated by the platform's Number Maintenance
        // subsystem during the insert pipeline; on most platform releases
        // the number is already visible on the original GlideRecord by
        // the time insert() returns, but a fresh GlideRecord.get(sys_id)
        // is the documented defensive pattern that works across all
        // releases (Yokohama and later per AAP Section 0.6.1).
        //
        // The newSysId used here is the value returned by insert() in the
        // line above - it is NOT a hardcoded sys_id literal, so this
        // GlideRecord.get(newSysId) call complies with the AAP Section
        // 0.7.2 no-hardcoded-sys_id constraint.
        var savedGr = new GlideRecord('x_casemgmt_case');
        if (!savedGr.get(newSysId)) {
            gs.error('CasePortalService.submitCase: post-insert lookup failed for sys_id=' + newSysId);
            return { error: 'Submission failed.' };
        }

        // Return ONLY the auto-generated number - no other fields, no
        // sys_id, no audit fields. The portal confirmation widget
        // (../portal/widgets/sp_widget_x_casemgmt_case_confirmation_widget.xml)
        // displays this number to the requester so they can later look up
        // their case via the status page.
        return { number: String(savedGr.getValue('number')) };
    },

    /**
     * Anonymous case status lookup entry point.
     *
     * Whitelist-only field return per AAP Section 0.7.4:
     *   - Looks up by case number (CASE0000001 style; the public-facing
     *     identifier returned by submitCase).
     *   - Returns ONLY: status, subject, opened_date.
     *   - NEVER returns: assigned_group, assigned_agent, description,
     *     closed_date, requester_name, requester_email, priority, type,
     *     pending_reason, sys_id, sys_created_by, sys_created_on,
     *     sys_updated_by, sys_updated_on, or any other field. The
     *     three-field whitelist is the privacy perimeter for anonymous
     *     lookups - returning the full record would expose internal
     *     assignment data and PII that the requester themselves
     *     supplied at submission time.
     *   - Returns null when no case matches. The calling scripted REST
     *     endpoint translates null into the HTTP 404 not-found response
     *     whose verbatim body is specified in AAP Section 0.7.4. The
     *     user-facing not-found message is INTENTIONALLY absent from this
     *     Script Include's runtime path - it is the REST endpoint's
     *     responsibility to surface that message.
     *
     * Robust input handling per Rule 9 of the agent prompt: gracefully
     * handle empty strings, whitespace-only strings, and non-string
     * inputs without throwing.
     *
     * @param {String} number - case number (e.g., 'CASE0000001'). Any
     *     leading/trailing whitespace is stripped before query.
     * @return {Object|null} { status, subject, opened_date } when a case
     *     with the given number is found, or null when no case matches
     *     (including when the number argument is null, undefined, empty,
     *     non-string, or whitespace-only).
     */
    lookupCase: function(number) {
        // Defensive null/type check. The scripted REST endpoint passes
        // through whatever the caller supplied as the 'number' query
        // parameter; a missing parameter yields undefined, an empty
        // parameter yields '', and the platform may sometimes coerce
        // numeric-looking strings into numbers. All of these should
        // produce a clean "not found" response without throwing.
        if (number === null || number === undefined) {
            return null;
        }
        // Coerce to string defensively before calling .trim() - the
        // string primitive may be received as a Number or other type.
        var trimmed = String(number).trim();
        if (trimmed === '') {
            return null;
        }

        var caseGr = new GlideRecord('x_casemgmt_case');
        // Query by the public-facing 'number' field, NOT by sys_id. The
        // case number is the stable human-readable identifier shown to
        // the requester on the submission confirmation; it is the only
        // identifier the requester ever sees, so it is the only key the
        // lookup endpoint accepts. This compliance with the AAP Section
        // 0.7.2 no-hardcoded-sys_id constraint is also a privacy win:
        // anonymous callers cannot probe the system by guessing
        // 32-character hex sys_id values.
        caseGr.addQuery('number', trimmed);
        // setLimit(1) is a defensive optimization - the case number is
        // a unique field per the auto-numbering generator, so at most
        // one row can match. Setting the limit eliminates any potential
        // for a misconfiguration to return multiple rows and tells the
        // database engine to stop after the first hit.
        caseGr.setLimit(1);
        caseGr.query();

        if (!caseGr.next()) {
            // No case with the given number was found. Return null; the
            // caller (the scripted REST operation script) translates
            // null into the HTTP 404 response whose verbatim body is
            // specified in AAP Section 0.7.4. We deliberately do NOT
            // include that verbatim text in this Script Include - the
            // REST endpoint owns the user-facing message, and embedding
            // the literal here would create a maintenance hazard if the
            // message ever needed to be reworded (which would then
            // require a schema/Update-Set re-export rather than just a
            // REST endpoint update).
            return null;
        }

        // Whitelisted output fields per AAP Section 0.7.4. EXACTLY three
        // fields are exposed to anonymous lookup callers:
        //
        //   - status: lets the requester see if their case is still
        //     Draft, has progressed to Open / In Progress / Pending /
        //     Resolved, or has been Closed.
        //   - subject: lets the requester confirm they're looking up the
        //     correct case (the requester chose this string at
        //     submission time, so echoing it back confirms identity
        //     without exposing other-party content).
        //   - opened_date: lets the requester compute how long the case
        //     has been open. Note: opened_date is auto-set on insert
        //     by the before-insert business rule
        //     ../business_rules/x_casemgmt_set_opened_date.xml.
        //
        // The String() coercion normalizes the GlideElement primitive
        // values into plain strings (so JSON.stringify on the result
        // produces clean JSON without any GlideElement object metadata).
        // The `|| ''` defaults handle the rare edge case where a column
        // is unexpectedly null-valued at runtime (e.g., a partially-
        // initialized seed-data row); empty strings are safer than null
        // in JSON responses to widget code that may not handle null
        // gracefully.
        return {
            status:      String(caseGr.getValue('status') || ''),
            subject:     String(caseGr.getValue('subject') || ''),
            opened_date: String(caseGr.getValue('opened_date') || '')
        };
    },

    /**
     * Class-name marker. ServiceNow's Class.create() pattern conventionally
     * exposes a `type` property whose value matches the class name (without
     * the scope prefix). This is used by the platform's introspection
     * tooling and by some debug logging. It MUST be 'CasePortalService'
     * (NOT 'x_casemgmt_CasePortalService') - the scope prefix lives only in
     * the <api_name> element above, not in the class name itself.
     */
    type: 'CasePortalService'
};
]]></script>
        <sys_class_name>sys_script_include</sys_class_name>
        <sys_created_by>admin</sys_created_by>
        <sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on>
        <sys_id>95e90fa18471e42875f5f956ec7949d1</sys_id>
        <sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count>
        <sys_name>CasePortalService</sys_name>
        <sys_package display_value="Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">x_casemgmt</sys_package>
        <sys_policy/>
        <sys_scope display_value="Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope>

        <sys_updated_by>admin</sys_updated_by>

    </sys_script_include>
</record_update>

sys_update_xml.name: x_casemgmt_block_draft_backtransition
sys_update_xml.payload:
<record_update table="sys_script">
    <sys_script action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE">
        <abort_action>false</abort_action>
        <access>package_private</access>
        <action_delete>false</action_delete>
        <action_insert>false</action_insert>
        <action_query>false</action_query>
        <action_update>true</action_update>
        <active>true</active>
        <add_message>false</add_message>
        <advanced>true</advanced>
        <change_fields>false</change_fields>
        <client_callable>false</client_callable>
        <collection>x_casemgmt_case</collection>
        <condition/>
        <description>Before-update guard on x_casemgmt_case: blocks any transition from a non-Draft status back to Draft. When current.status === 'Draft' AND previous.status !== 'Draft' AND previous.status !== '', delegates to x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator.validateNoBacktransition(previousStatus, newStatus) and surfaces the verbatim error message 'Cases cannot be returned to Draft.' via gs.addErrorMessage() + current.setAbortAction(true) when the validator returns {ok: false}. Per AAP Sections 0.5.5 (transition matrix row 7: 'Any -> Draft: PROHIBITED') and 0.7.4 (verbatim error message - non-negotiable). Order=200 is the SECOND-HIGHEST priority before-update rule in this scoped application; runs AFTER block_terminal_closed (order=100) so terminal-Closed cases short-circuit before this guard, and BEFORE all subsequent housekeeping rules (validate_assigned_agent_membership at 300, clear_pending_reason_on_inprogress at 400, set_closed_date at 500). The Script Include is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the verbatim error message; this BR contains zero inline error strings. action_insert=false because Draft is the legitimate initial status (per dictionary default_value); only the BACK-transition from a non-Draft state is forbidden. Defensive previous-null guard handles async/system contexts where previous can be null. Skip-if-no-change guard (prevStatus === newStatus) avoids unnecessary Script Include instantiation on non-status-changing updates. Type-agnostic: fires for both General Inquiry and Complaint case types. Defense in depth: the per-type Flow Designer flows do NOT enforce this rule, so this BR is the only enforcer for direct DB modifications via Table API, scripted REST, GlideRecord scripts, and bulk imports. Contains zero gs.eventQueue() calls per the email-disabled constraint and zero hardcoded sys_id literals.</description>
        <execute_function>false</execute_function>
        <filter_condition/>
        <is_rest>false</is_rest>
        <message/>
        <name>x_casemgmt_block_draft_backtransition</name>
        <order>200</order>
        <priority>100</priority>
        <rest_method/>
        <rest_method_text/>
        <rest_service/>
        <rest_service_text/>
        <rest_variables/>
        <role_conditions/>
        <script><![CDATA[(function executeRule(current, previous /*null when async*/) {
    // Per AAP Section 0.5.5 (transition matrix row 7):
    //     "Any -> Draft: PROHIBITED"
    //     Failure surface: "Cases cannot be returned to Draft."
    //
    // Per AAP Section 0.7.4: the literal text "Cases cannot be returned to
    // Draft." is the VERBATIM, NON-NEGOTIABLE error message surfaced when
    // this guard fires. Character-for-character: capital "C", capital "D",
    // trailing period, exact wording. The message lives ONCE in the Script
    // Include's validateNoBacktransition() return; this BR reads it from
    // result.error and never inlines it.
    //
    // Order=200 makes this the SECOND before-update rule in this scoped
    // application. Order=100 (block_terminal_closed) runs first to catch
    // the more aggressive Closed-terminal prohibition; once that rule has
    // confirmed the case is not Closed, this rule fires at order=200 to
    // catch the more specific Any->Draft case. Subsequent rules
    // (validate_assigned_agent_membership at 300,
    // clear_pending_reason_on_inprogress at 400, set_closed_date at 500)
    // are short-circuited when this rule aborts via setAbortAction(true).
    //
    // Delegates to x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator.validateNoBacktransition()
    // which returns { ok: true } when the transition is allowed, or
    // { ok: false, error: 'Cases cannot be returned to Draft.' } when
    // transitioning TO Draft from a non-Draft state (prev !== '' &&
    // prev !== 'Draft' && next === 'Draft'). The Script Include is the
    // single source of truth for the verbatim message and the prohibited
    // -transition matrix; this BR consumes its return shape and surfaces
    // the error.
    //
    // ArkCase source-side analog: ChangeCaseFileStateService at
    // acm-plugins/acm-default-plugins/acm-case-file-plugin/src/main/java/com/
    // armedia/acm/plugins/casefile/service/ChangeCaseFileStateService.java
    // handled state changes via changeCaseState() (line 95: setStatus)
    // without enforcing a Draft-backtransition rule. Backtransition behavior
    // was implicit in Activiti BPMN process definitions and queue handlers
    // (e.g., CaseFileQueueHandler.java set status to ACTIVE pre-save). This
    // BR makes the rule EXPLICIT at the data layer, hardening the
    // state-machine contract per AAP Section 0.5.5.

    // Defensive previous-null guard: the `previous` GlideRecord is null in
    // certain async/system contexts (scheduled jobs invoking
    // GlideRecord.update(), some bulk import scenarios, server-side script
    // paths that call GlideRecord.updateMultiple()). If there is no previous
    // state, no transition can be detected, and the rule does nothing.
    if (!previous) {
        return;
    }

    // String() cast normalizes the GlideElement to a primitive string for
    // safe === comparison; without the cast, GlideElement-vs-string equality
    // can behave inconsistently across releases. The Title Case literal
    // 'Draft' (5 chars, single word) is the verbatim choice value from
    // ../choices/sys_choice_case_status.xml per AAP Section 0.5.7. Variants
    // like 'DRAFT' (uppercase, ArkCase Java legacy from CaseFile.java
    // @PrePersist hook), 'draft' (lowercase), or 'Drafting' (extended)
    // would silently never match.
    var prevStatus = String(previous.status);
    var newStatus = String(current.status);

    // Skip if status didn't change - this rule only cares about transitions.
    // Avoids unnecessary Script Include instantiation on the vast majority
    // of UPDATE operations (those that don't change the status field).
    if (prevStatus === newStatus) {
        return;
    }

    // Only fire when transitioning TO Draft from a non-Draft non-empty state.
    // Three conditions, all required:
    //   (1) newStatus === 'Draft'           - we're transitioning toward Draft
    //   (2) prevStatus !== 'Draft'          - we're moving FROM a non-Draft state
    //   (3) prevStatus !== ''               - defensive: empty previousStatus
    //                                         on a brand-new record can't reach
    //                                         this BR because action_insert is
    //                                         false; this guard is belt-and-
    //                                         suspenders for unusual contexts
    //                                         where the platform might emit an
    //                                         empty-string previous.status on a
    //                                         pseudo-update.
    // This BR's pre-check is redundant with the Script Include's authoritative
    // matrix but acts as a fast-path filter to avoid Script Include
    // instantiation cost on the vast majority of updates. Defense in depth:
    // if this pre-check were ever loosened, the Script Include's matrix
    // would still produce the correct result.
    if (newStatus === 'Draft' && prevStatus !== 'Draft' && prevStatus !== '') {
        // Resolve the Script Include via the standard scoped reference syntax.
        // The `x_casemgmt` portion is the scope's vendor_prefix from
        // ../app/sys_app/x_casemgmt_case_management.xml; the
        // `CaseTransitionValidator` portion is the api_name of the Script
        // Include. NO sys_id literal - the resolution is by scoped class
        // name only.
        var validator = new x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator();
        var result = validator.validateNoBacktransition(prevStatus, newStatus);
        if (!result.ok) {
            // gs.addErrorMessage(result.error) surfaces the verbatim message
            // at the top of the form when the user attempts the save through
            // the UI, and is captured in the API response when the update
            // arrives via Table API or scripted REST. The string is read from
            // result.error - never inlined here - so the verbatim wording
            // contract is enforced by the Script Include alone.
            gs.addErrorMessage(result.error);
            // current.setAbortAction(true) cancels the database write. Both
            // the gs.addErrorMessage() and setAbortAction(true) calls are
            // required: the former produces a visible error to the caller,
            // the latter prevents the write from being persisted. Without
            // setAbortAction(true), the message would appear but the row
            // would still update; without gs.addErrorMessage(), the write
            // would be silently rejected with no visible failure.
            current.setAbortAction(true);
        }
    }
})(current, previous);
]]></script>

The Script Include is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the verbatim error message; this BR contains zero inline error strings. action_insert=false because new cases always start at Draft (per dictionary default_value); only updates on already-Closed rows trigger this guard. Defensive previous-null guard handles async/system contexts where previous can be null. Script Include's validateNoBacktransition returns {ok: true} for the no-op Closed -> Closed case (status field unchanged), so non-status edits to a Closed row pass through; only actual transitions out of Closed are blocked. Type-agnostic: fires for both General Inquiry and Complaint case types. Defense in depth: the per-type Flow Designer flows do NOT enforce this rule, so this BR is the only enforcer for direct DB modifications via Table API, scripted REST, GlideRecord scripts, and bulk imports. Contains zero gs.eventQueue() calls per the email-disabled constraint and zero hardcoded sys_id literals.</description>

        <script><![CDATA[(function executeRule(current, previous /*null when async*/) {
    // Per AAP Section 0.5.5 (transition matrix row 8):
    //     "Closed -> *: PROHIBITED -- terminal state"
    //     Failure surface: "Closed cases are terminal and cannot be modified."
    //
    // Per AAP Section 0.7.4: the literal text "Closed cases are terminal and
    // cannot be modified." is the VERBATIM, NON-NEGOTIABLE error message
    // surfaced when this guard fires. Character-for-character: capital "C",
    // trailing period, exact wording. The message lives ONCE in the Script

    //
    // Order=100 makes this the FIRST/HIGHEST-PRIORITY before-update rule
    // in this scoped application. Subsequent rules

    // invalid update, and skipping the downstream rules saves database
    // queries and CPU.
    //

    // when transitioning OUT of Closed (i.e., prev === 'Closed' &&
    // next !== 'Closed' && next !== ''). The Script Include is the single
    // source of truth for the verbatim message and the prohibited-transition
    // matrix; this BR consumes its return shape and surfaces the error.
    //
    // ArkCase source-side analog: ChangeCaseFileStateService at
    // acm-plugins/acm-default-plugins/acm-case-file-plugin/src/main/java/com/
    // armedia/acm/plugins/casefile/service/ChangeCaseFileStateService.java
    // handled state changes via changeCaseState() (line 95: setStatus,
    // line 99: setClosed for CLOSED transitions) but did NOT enforce a
    // "Closed is terminal" rule - the ArkCase service would happily transition
    // a Closed case to any other status. Terminal-state behavior was implicit
    // in Activiti BPMN process definitions and queue handlers. This BR makes
    // the rule EXPLICIT at the data layer, hardening the state-machine contract
    // per AAP Section 0.5.5.

    // Defensive previous-null guard: the `previous` GlideRecord is null in
    // certain async/system contexts (scheduled jobs invoking
    // GlideRecord.update(), some bulk import scenarios, server-side script
    // paths that call GlideRecord.updateMultiple()). If there is no previous
    // state, no terminal state can be detected, and the rule does nothing.
    if (!previous) {
        return;
    }

    // safe === comparison; without the cast, GlideElement-vs-string equality
    // can behave inconsistently across releases. The Title Case literal
    // 'Closed' (6 chars, single word) is the verbatim choice value from
    // ../choices/sys_choice_case_status.xml per AAP Section 0.5.7. Variants
    // like 'CLOSED' (uppercase, ArkCase Java legacy), 'closed' (lowercase),
    // or 'Close' (no trailing 'd') would silently never match.
    var prevStatus = String(previous.status);
    var newStatus = String(current.status);

    // Only fire when previous.status is Closed. The Script Include returns
    // { ok: false, error: 'Closed cases are terminal and cannot be modified.' }
    // when prev === 'Closed' && next !== 'Closed' && next !== ''. The Script
    // Include returns { ok: true } for the no-op Closed -> Closed case (status
    // unchanged - non-status edits to a Closed row are not blocked here; if
    // additional per-field immutability is required, dictionary read_only
    // flags or field-level ACLs are the right mechanism).
    if (prevStatus === 'Closed') {
        // Resolve the Script Include via the standard scoped reference syntax.
        // The `x_casemgmt` portion is the scope's vendor_prefix from
        // ../app/sys_app/x_casemgmt_case_management.xml; the `CaseTransitionValidator`
        // portion is the api_name of the Script Include. NO sys_id literal -
        // the resolution is by scoped class name only.
        var validator = new x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator();
        var result = validator.validateNoBacktransition(prevStatus, newStatus);
        if (!result.ok) {
            // gs.addErrorMessage(result.error) surfaces the verbatim message
            // at the top of the form when the user attempts the save through
            // the UI, and is captured in the API response when the update
            // arrives via Table API or scripted REST. The string is read from
            // result.error - never inlined here - so the verbatim wording
            // contract is enforced by the Script Include alone.
            gs.addErrorMessage(result.error);
            // current.setAbortAction(true) cancels the database write. Both
            // the gs.addErrorMessage() and setAbortAction(true) calls are
            // required: the former produces a visible error to the caller,
            // the latter prevents the write from being persisted. Without
            // setAbortAction(true), the message would appear but the row
            // would still update; without gs.addErrorMessage(), the write
            // would be silently rejected with no visible failure.
            current.setAbortAction(true);
        }
    }
})(current, previous);
]]></script>

        <description>Before-insert on x_casemgmt_case: sets current.opened_date = gs.nowDateTime() when not already populated. Replaces ArkCase CaseFile.@PrePersist beforeInsert() audit hook from acm-plugins/acm-default-plugins/acm-case-file-plugin/src/main/java/com/armedia/acm/plugins/casefile/model/CaseFile.java. Per AAP Section 0.5.7 (opened_date Auto-set on creation). Defensive: respects pre-set values from seed data and other authoritative callers via current.opened_date.nil() guard. Fires in all contexts (form, Table API, scripted REST, seed scripts) because is_rest=false. Order=100 ensures the field is populated early in the before-insert phase. Contains zero gs.eventQueue() calls per the email-disabled constraint.</description>
        <execute_function>false</execute_function>
        <filter_condition/>
        <is_rest>false</is_rest>

        <name>x_casemgmt_set_opened_date</name>
        <order>100</order>
        <priority>100</priority>
        <rest_method/>
        <rest_method_text/>
        <rest_service/>
        <rest_service_text/>
        <rest_variables/>

        <script><![CDATA[(function executeRule(current, previous /*null when async*/) {
    // ServiceNow-native equivalent of ArkCase CaseFile.@PrePersist beforeInsert()
    // (acm-plugins/acm-default-plugins/acm-case-file-plugin/src/main/java/com/
    //  armedia/acm/plugins/casefile/model/CaseFile.java, lines 307-316).
    //
    // Per AAP Section 0.5.7: opened_date is "DateTime, Auto-set on creation".
    //
    // Defensive .nil() guard: respect pre-set values from authoritative callers.
    // This is critical for the seed-data demos in
    // ../seed-data/cases/x_casemgmt_case_demo_*.xml which explicitly set
    // synthetic timestamps spanning the past 30 days so the "Cases opened
    // (30 days)" single-score widget on the Manager View dashboard
    // (../reports/x_casemgmt_cases_opened_30d.xml) has non-zero data on a
    // freshly-imported PDI. Without this guard, the seeded timestamps would
    // be overwritten with gs.nowDateTime() at import time and every demo
    // case would appear to be opened on import day.
    //
    // For organic inserts (form submissions, Table API calls, portal scripted
    // REST submissions, ad-hoc admin scripts) where opened_date is not
    // pre-populated, the script populates the field with the current platform
    // time so downstream reports and the portal status lookup never see a
    // null opened_date.
    if (current.opened_date.nil()) {
        current.opened_date = new GlideDateTime();
    }
})(current, previous);
]]></script>

        <collection>x_casemgmt_case</collection>
        <condition/>
        <description>Before-update on x_casemgmt_case: when previous.status == 'Resolved' AND current.status == 'Closed', sets current.closed_date = gs.nowDateTime() if not already populated. Replaces ArkCase ChangeCaseFileStateService.changeCaseState() retval.setClosed(now) (line 99 in acm-plugins/acm-default-plugins/acm-case-file-plugin/src/main/java/com/armedia/acm/plugins/casefile/service/ChangeCaseFileStateService.java). Per AAP Section 0.5.5 (Resolved->Closed auto-sets closed_date) and AAP Section 0.5.7 (closed_date DateTime, Auto-set on Close transition). Order=500 ensures this rule runs LAST among before-update rules so it only fires after all transition guards (block_terminal_closed, block_draft_backtransition, validate_assigned_agent_membership, clear_pending_reason_on_inprogress) have passed. Defensive .nil() guard preserves authoritative pre-set values from seed data and the validate_closed_transition Flow Designer subflow. Defense in depth with the subflow is intentional - this BR catches direct DB updates (Table API, scripted REST, GlideRecord scripts), the subflow catches interactive transitions through the form/UI. Contains zero gs.eventQueue() calls per the email-disabled constraint.</description>
        <execute_function>false</execute_function>
        <filter_condition/>
        <is_rest>false</is_rest>
        <message/>
        <name>x_casemgmt_set_closed_date</name>
        <order>500</order>
        <priority>100</priority>
        <rest_method/>
        <rest_method_text/>
        <rest_service/>
        <rest_service_text/>
        <rest_variables/>
        <role_conditions/>
        <script><![CDATA[(function executeRule(current, previous /*null when async*/) {
    // ServiceNow-native equivalent of ArkCase
    // ChangeCaseFileStateService.changeCaseState() line 99:
    //     if ("CLOSED".equals(newState)) { retval.setClosed(now); }
    // (acm-plugins/acm-default-plugins/acm-case-file-plugin/src/main/java/com/
    //  armedia/acm/plugins/casefile/service/ChangeCaseFileStateService.java)
    //
    // Per AAP Section 0.5.5: Resolved -> Closed transition auto-sets closed_date.
    // Per AAP Section 0.5.7: closed_date is "DateTime, Auto-set on Close transition".
    //
    // This BR runs alongside the Flow Designer subflow
    // ../flows/sub_flows/validate_closed_transition.xml; the redundancy is
    // intentional - this BR catches direct DB modifications (Table API,
    // scripted REST, GlideRecord scripts, bulk imports), the flow catches
    // interactive transitions through the form/UI.
    //
    // Order=500 ensures this rule runs LAST among before-update rules; if
    // any earlier guard aborted the action (block_terminal_closed at
    // order=100, block_draft_backtransition at order=200,
    // validate_assigned_agent_membership at order=300,
    // clear_pending_reason_on_inprogress at order=400), this BR is skipped.
    // We never stamp closed_date on a transition that's about to be
    // rejected.
    //
    // Defensive previous-null guard: the `previous` GlideRecord is null in
    // certain async/system contexts. If there is no previous state, no
    // transition can be detected, and the rule does nothing. The String()
    // cast normalizes the GlideElement to a primitive string for safe
    // === comparison; without the cast, GlideElement-vs-string equality
    // can behave inconsistently across releases.
    var prevStatus = previous ? String(previous.status) : '';
    var newStatus = String(current.status);

    // Verbatim Title Case status values per AAP Section 0.5.7 and the
    // sibling choice list ../choices/sys_choice_case_status.xml. The
    // labels ARE the stored values - ServiceNow Choice fields persist
    // the LABEL string by default, not an integer ID.
    if (prevStatus === 'Resolved' && newStatus === 'Closed') {
        // Defensive .nil() guard: respect pre-set values from the
        // Flow Designer subflow (which fires in the same transaction
        // for interactive transitions and may have already stamped
        // the column) and from any future seed-data path that updates
        // an already-loaded case from Resolved to Closed. Without this
        // guard, a value already written by the subflow would be
        // overwritten by gs.nowDateTime() at this rule's execution
        // point - harmless in practice (both writers produce the same
        // millisecond-precision timestamp within a single transaction)
        // but unnecessary and slightly less clear in audit logs.
        if (current.closed_date.nil()) {
            current.closed_date = new GlideDateTime();
        }
    }
})(current, previous);
]]></script>
