sys_update_xml.name: x_casemgmt_validate_assigned_agent_membership
sys_update_xml.payload:
<record_update table="sys_script">
    <sys_script action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE">
        <abort_action>false</abort_action>
        <access>package_private</access>
        <action_delete>false</action_delete>
        <action_insert>true</action_insert>
        <action_query>false</action_query>
        <action_update>true</action_update>
        <active>true</active>
        <add_message>false</add_message>
        <advanced>true</advanced>
        <change_fields>false</change_fields>
        <client_callable>false</client_callable>
        <collection>x_casemgmt_case</collection>
        <condition/>
        <description>Before-insert/update on x_casemgmt_case: when assigned_agent and assigned_group are both populated, validates that the agent is a member of the group via x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator.isAgentInGroup(). On failure, surfaces the form-level error 'Assigned agent must be a member of the assigned group.' via gs.addErrorMessage() + current.setAbortAction(true). Per AAP Sections 0.5.5 (transition matrix row 2: Open -> In Progress: 'assigned_agent populated AND member of assigned_group') and 0.5.7 (assigned_agent constraint: 'Optional; must be member of assigned_group'). Order=300 places this rule THIRD in the before-rule chain on x_casemgmt_case, after block_terminal_closed (100) and block_draft_backtransition (200) and before clear_pending_reason_on_inprogress (400) and set_closed_date (500); running after the prohibition guards is a deliberate performance optimization so we don't run the sys_user_grmember GlideRecord lookup on transitions that will be rejected anyway. Dual-triggered (action_insert=true AND action_update=true) because a manager (or seed script) may assign agent and group at case-creation time via a single Table API call, not just through subsequent updates. Skip conditions: (a) either agent or group is empty (b) neither field changed since previous - avoid redundant queries on non-assignment-touching updates. Defensive previous-null guard: on insert previous is null and both change-detection flags evaluate true so the membership is always validated for new rows. Type-agnostic: fires for both General Inquiry and Complaint case types because the membership constraint applies regardless of case type. Defense in depth: validate_inprogress_transition subflow makes the same check at the workflow layer; this BR catches direct DB writes bypassing the flow. The error message wording is NOT prescribed verbatim by AAP Section 0.7.4 (which lists only four verbatim messages); the chosen wording is consistent with the prompt's tone and the AAP's own narrative wording. Contains zero gs.eventQueue() calls per the email-disabled constraint and zero hardcoded sys_id literals (runtime sys_id comparisons via .toString() are platform-canonical and permitted).</description>
        <execute_function>false</execute_function>
        <filter_condition/>
        <is_rest>false</is_rest>
        <message/>
        <name>x_casemgmt_validate_assigned_agent_membership</name>
        <order>300</order>
        <priority>100</priority>
        <rest_method/>
        <rest_method_text/>
        <rest_service/>
        <rest_service_text/>
        <rest_variables/>
        <role_conditions/>
        <script><![CDATA[(function executeRule(current, previous /*null when async*/) {
    // Per AAP Section 0.5.7 (x_casemgmt_case schema row 10):
    //     "assigned_agent | Reference -> sys_user | Optional; must be
    //      member of assigned_group"
    //
    // Per AAP Section 0.5.5 (transition matrix row 2):
    //     | From | To          | Required condition                       | Failure handling          |
    //     | Open | In Progress | assigned_agent populated AND member of   | Surface form-level error  |
    //     |      |             | assigned_group                           |                           |
    //
    // The membership check is delegated to
    //     new x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator().isAgentInGroup(agentSysId, groupSysId)
    // which performs a sys_user_grmember GlideRecord lookup and returns a
    // plain boolean. The Script Include is the single source of truth for
    // the membership query so the same logic is reusable across this BR,
    // the validate_inprogress_transition Flow Designer subflow, ACL
    // conditions for child case_task and case_party rows, and the
    // seed-script preflight checks. Inlining a GlideRecord('sys_user_grmember')
    // query here would create a second source of truth and risk the two
    // implementations diverging on edge cases.
    //
    // Order=300 places this rule THIRD in the before-rule chain on
    // x_casemgmt_case, after block_terminal_closed (order=100, blocks any
    // edit to a Closed case) and block_draft_backtransition (order=200,
    // blocks any rewind to Draft). The chain order is a deliberate
    // performance optimization: invalid transitions short-circuit at the
    // earlier orders via setAbortAction(true) and we never reach this rule's
    // GlideRecord query for them. Cases that survive to order=300 have a
    // legitimate forward-transition or non-status edit, so the membership
    // check is appropriate. Subsequent rules
    // (clear_pending_reason_on_inprogress at order=400, set_closed_date at
    // order=500) are short-circuited if THIS rule aborts.
    //
    // ArkCase source-side analog: there was no direct equivalent at the JPA
    // entity layer in
    //   acm-plugins/acm-default-plugins/acm-case-file-plugin/src/main/java/
    //     com/armedia/acm/plugins/casefile/model/CaseFile.java
    // CaseFile modeled assignment via an AcmParticipant collection (lines
    // 192, 336-340, 880-908) where ASSIGNEE and OWNING_GROUP participant
    // types coexisted on the case but the relational integrity between an
    // assignee and the owning group was enforced indirectly through the
    // LDAP/AD organizational structure - if a user existed in LDAP they
    // could be assigned regardless of their group membership. The
    // ServiceNow target makes this rule EXPLICIT at the data layer via
    // this BR plus the Script Include's isAgentInGroup() helper - a
    // deliberate hardening of the case assignment contract. This is a
    // TARGET-SIDE AUTHORED rule with no byte-for-byte source analog.

    // Read the assigned_agent and assigned_group sys_id values from the
    // platform-injected `current` GlideRecord. The .toString() coercion
    // normalizes the GlideElement reference field to its underlying sys_id
    // string. Without explicit coercion, the GlideElement instance auto-
    // converts in some contexts but not others (string concatenation =
    // string conversion; equality comparison via === = identity comparison;
    // method-argument passing = pass-by-value of the underlying string
    // for primitive comparisons but pass-by-reference of the GlideElement
    // wrapper for complex operations). The downstream isAgentInGroup()
    // method explicitly handles String() coercion of its arguments and
    // GlideRecord.addQuery() accepts both forms, but explicit .toString()
    // here is the platform-canonical defensive pattern and avoids any
    // wrapper-vs-primitive ambiguity downstream.
    var agent = current.assigned_agent.toString();
    var group = current.assigned_group.toString();

    // Skip if either field is empty. The AAP defines assigned_agent as
    // optional (Section 0.5.7: "Optional"); a case without an assigned
    // agent is a valid state (e.g., Draft cases, Open cases waiting for
    // agent assignment). assigned_group is mandatory only on the
    // Open transition (per dictionary mandatory_on_open=true at
    // ../dictionary/x_casemgmt_case_assigned_group.xml) - that mandatory
    // requirement is enforced separately by the form-level mandatory flag
    // and the validate_open_transition subflow, NOT by this BR.
    // This BR's responsibility is narrow: validate the membership
    // RELATIONSHIP when both fields are present. If either field is
    // absent, the relationship cannot be validated and the rule does
    // nothing.
    if (!agent || !group) {
        return;
    }

    // Skip if neither agent nor group changed (avoid redundant queries on
    // every save, including subsequent updates that touch only other
    // fields like description, priority, or status). For a case that
    // travels through the full state-machine
    //   Draft -> Open -> In Progress -> Pending -> In Progress -> Resolved -> Closed
    // the assignment fields typically change at most twice (once when the
    // group is set on Draft -> Open, once when the agent is set on
    // Open -> In Progress). This guard ensures the BR runs the
    // sys_user_grmember query at most twice across the full lifecycle
    // rather than five times.
    //
    // On INSERT, `previous` is null (no prior state), so the ternary's
    // !previous branch evaluates true for both flags - the BR always
    // validates the membership on a brand-new row. This is the correct
    // semantic: a manager creating a case AND assigning both group and
    // agent in a single operation must have the assignment validated
    // before the row is persisted, otherwise an invalid agent-group
    // pairing could be created and only caught on the first subsequent
    // update.
    var agentChanged = !previous || String(previous.assigned_agent) !== agent;
    var groupChanged = !previous || String(previous.assigned_group) !== group;
    if (!agentChanged && !groupChanged) {
        return;
    }

    // Resolve the Script Include via the standard scoped reference syntax.
    // The `x_casemgmt` portion is the scope's vendor_prefix from
    // ../app/sys_app/x_casemgmt_case_management.xml; the
    // `CaseTransitionValidator` portion is the api_name of the Script
    // Include declared in
    // ../script_includes/x_casemgmt_CaseTransitionValidator.xml at
    // <api_name>x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator</api_name>. NO sys_id
    // literal - the resolution is by scoped class name only.
    var validator = new x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator();

    // Call isAgentInGroup(userSysId, groupSysId). The Script Include's
    // method (line 656 in CaseTransitionValidator.xml) returns a plain
    // boolean: true when at least one sys_user_grmember row links the
    // given user to the given group, false otherwise (including when
    // either argument is null/empty/whitespace). The boolean shape
    // (rather than the {ok, error} pair used by validateNoBacktransition
    // and the canTransitionTo* family) is intentional: isAgentInGroup is
    // a simple yes/no membership predicate reusable from contexts that
    // have no error-message surface (e.g., ACL condition expressions).
    // The form-level error string is owned by THIS BR and surfaced via
    // gs.addErrorMessage(...) below.
    if (!validator.isAgentInGroup(agent, group)) {
        // gs.addErrorMessage('...') surfaces the form-level error at the
        // top of the case form when the user attempts the save through
        // the UI, and is captured in the API response when the update
        // arrives via Table API or scripted REST. Per AAP Section 0.7.1:
        // "Surface all blocking errors on the form. Invalid transition
        // attempts MUST produce a blocking error message visible on the
        // form - silent failures or post-save error logs are
        // unacceptable."
        //
        // Per AAP Section 0.7.4, only four error messages are verbatim
        // (non-negotiable): "All tasks must be closed before resolving
        // this case.", "Cases cannot be returned to Draft.", "Closed
        // cases are terminal and cannot be modified.", and "No case
        // found with that number." This rule's message is NOT in that
        // list, so the wording here is target-side authored. The chosen
        // string is consistent with the prompt's tone and the AAP's own
        // narrative wording in Section 0.5.7 ("Optional; must be member
        // of assigned_group").
        gs.addErrorMessage('Assigned agent must be a member of the assigned group.');

        // current.setAbortAction(true) cancels the database write. Both
        // the gs.addErrorMessage() and setAbortAction(true) calls are
        // required: the former produces a visible error to the caller,
        // the latter prevents the write from being persisted. Without
        // setAbortAction(true), the message would appear but the row
        // would still update with the invalid agent-group pairing;
        // without gs.addErrorMessage(), the write would be silently
        // rejected with no visible failure and no diagnostic message
        // for the caller.
        current.setAbortAction(true);
    }
})(current, previous);
]]></script>
        <sys_class_name>sys_script</sys_class_name>
        <sys_created_by>admin</sys_created_by>
        <sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on>
        <sys_domain>global</sys_domain>
        <sys_domain_path>/</sys_domain_path>
        <sys_id>8136e6a730a2da3c4c36038f572c4269</sys_id>
        <sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count>
        <sys_name>x_casemgmt_validate_assigned_agent_membership</sys_name>
        <sys_overrides/>
        <sys_package display_value="Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">x_casemgmt</sys_package>
        <sys_policy/>
        <sys_scope display_value="Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope>
        <sys_update_name>sys_script_x_casemgmt_validate_assigned_agent_membership</sys_update_name>
        <sys_updated_by>admin</sys_updated_by>
        <sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on>
        <template/>
        <when>before</when>
    </sys_script>
</record_update>

sys_update_xml.name: x_casemgmt_clear_pending_reason_on_inprogress
sys_update_xml.payload:
<record_update table="sys_script">
    <sys_script action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE">
        <abort_action>false</abort_action>
        <access>package_private</access>
        <action_delete>false</action_delete>
        <action_insert>false</action_insert>
        <action_query>false</action_query>
        <action_update>true</action_update>
        <active>true</active>
        <add_message>false</add_message>
        <advanced>true</advanced>
        <change_fields>false</change_fields>
        <client_callable>false</client_callable>
        <collection>x_casemgmt_case</collection>
        <condition/>
        <description>Before-update on x_casemgmt_case: when previous.status == 'Pending' AND current.status == 'In Progress', clears current.pending_reason (sets it to empty string). Per AAP Section 0.5.5 (Pending->In Progress: clears pending_reason). Order=400 ensures this rule runs after the transition guards (block_terminal_closed at order=100, block_draft_backtransition at order=200, validate_assigned_agent_membership at order=300) but before set_closed_date (order=500), so it only fires after all guards have approved the transition. Companion to ../flows/sub_flows/validate_pending_transition.xml which SETS pending_reason on the In Progress->Pending transition; this rule CLEARS it on the reverse transition. Type-agnostic: fires for both General Inquiry and Complaint case types since the Pending state is shared. Defensive previous-null guard handles async/system contexts where previous can be null. Contains zero gs.eventQueue() calls per the email-disabled constraint and zero GlideRecord lookups.</description>
        <execute_function>false</execute_function>
        <filter_condition/>
        <is_rest>false</is_rest>
        <message/>
        <name>x_casemgmt_clear_pending_reason_on_inprogress</name>
        <order>400</order>
        <priority>100</priority>
        <rest_method/>
        <rest_method_text/>
        <rest_service/>
        <rest_service_text/>
        <rest_variables/>
        <role_conditions/>
        <script><![CDATA[(function executeRule(current, previous /*null when async*/) {
    // Per AAP Section 0.5.5 verbatim:
    //     "Pending -> In Progress: None; clears pending_reason"
    //
    // The pending_reason field is SET by the Flow Designer subflow
    // ../flows/sub_flows/validate_pending_transition.xml when the case
    // transitions INTO Pending. When the case transitions OUT of Pending
    // back to In Progress, the previously stored reason is no longer
    // relevant and would be misleading on the form. This rule guarantees
    // the field is empty for any non-Pending case reached via the
    // Pending -> In Progress transition path.
    //
    // This BR has no ArkCase source-side analog. ArkCase did not have
    // a discrete Pending sub-state with a typed reason code; this is
    // target-side-only behavior introduced by the AAP design.
    //
    // Order=400 ensures this rule runs AFTER all transition guards
    // (block_terminal_closed at order=100, block_draft_backtransition at
    // order=200, validate_assigned_agent_membership at order=300) have
    // approved the transition, and BEFORE set_closed_date (order=500)
    // which handles the Resolved -> Closed side-effect. If any earlier
    // guard aborts the action, this rule is skipped (the platform
    // short-circuits the BR pipeline on abort) - which is correct,
    // because we never want to clear pending_reason on a transition
    // that's about to be rejected.
    //
    // Defensive previous-null guard: the `previous` GlideRecord is null
    // in certain async/system contexts. If there is no previous state,
    // no transition can be detected, and the rule does nothing. The
    // String() cast normalizes the GlideElement to a primitive string
    // for safe === comparison; without the cast, GlideElement-vs-string
    // equality can behave inconsistently across releases.
    var prevStatus = previous ? String(previous.status) : '';
    var newStatus = String(current.status);

    // Verbatim Title Case status values per AAP Section 0.5.7 and the
    // sibling choice list ../choices/sys_choice_case_status.xml. The
    // labels ARE the stored values - ServiceNow Choice fields persist
    // the LABEL string by default, not an integer ID. Note 'In Progress'
    // contains a literal SPACE in the middle (NOT 'In_Progress', NOT
    // 'InProgress', NOT 'in progress'). Misspelled variants would
    // silently never match and the rule would never fire - a critical
    // correctness concern that is encoded by these exact string literals.
    if (prevStatus === 'Pending' && newStatus === 'In Progress') {
        // The empty-string assignment is the canonical ServiceNow pattern
        // for clearing a Choice field's value. Per
        // ../dictionary/x_casemgmt_case_pending_reason.xml the field is
        // non-mandatory (mandatory=false), so clearing it is a legitimate
        // end-state - the row remains valid with an empty pending_reason
        // for any non-Pending status. The next time the case transitions
        // to Pending, the validate_pending_transition subflow will prompt
        // for a fresh reason and populate the field again.
        current.pending_reason = '';
    }
})(current, previous);
]]></script>
        <sys_class_name>sys_script</sys_class_name>
        <sys_created_by>admin</sys_created_by>
        <sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on>
        <sys_domain>global</sys_domain>
        <sys_domain_path>/</sys_domain_path>
        <sys_id>0943b10691d8ae86fd3c2fd6994eb693</sys_id>
        <sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count>
        <sys_name>x_casemgmt_clear_pending_reason_on_inprogress</sys_name>
        <sys_overrides/>
        <sys_package display_value="Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">x_casemgmt</sys_package>
        <sys_policy/>
        <sys_scope display_value="Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope>
        <sys_update_name>sys_script_x_casemgmt_clear_pending_reason_on_inprogress</sys_update_name>
        <sys_updated_by>admin</sys_updated_by>
        <sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on>
        <template/>
        <when>before</when>
    </sys_script>
</record_update>

sys_update_xml.name: x_casemgmt_enforce_forward_transitions
sys_update_xml.payload:
<record_update table="sys_script">
    <sys_script action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE">
        <abort_action>false</abort_action>
        <access>package_private</access>
        <action_delete>false</action_delete>
        <action_insert>false</action_insert>
        <action_query>false</action_query>
        <action_update>true</action_update>
        <active>true</active>
        <add_message>false</add_message>
        <advanced>true</advanced>
        <change_fields>false</change_fields>
        <client_callable>false</client_callable>
        <collection>x_casemgmt_case</collection>
        <condition/>
        <description>Before-update guard on x_casemgmt_case that enforces the forward-transition preconditions of the case state machine. On a status change it invokes the matching natively authored Flow Designer subflow (x_casemgmt.validate_open_transition, validate_in_progress_transition, validate_pending_transition, validate_resolved_transition, validate_closed_transition) synchronously with sn_fd.FlowAPI.getRunner().inForeground(), then re-evaluates the same gate against the in-flight record through x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator and, on failure, calls gs.addErrorMessage() with the verbatim blocking message plus current.setAbortAction(true) so the error surfaces on the form. Order 250 runs after the Closed-terminal (100) and Any-to-Draft (200) prohibition guards and before the side-effect rules (300/400/500).</description>
        <execute_function>false</execute_function>
        <filter_condition/>
        <is_rest>false</is_rest>
        <message/>
        <name>x_casemgmt_enforce_forward_transitions</name>
        <order>250</order>
        <priority>100</priority>
        <rest_method/>
        <rest_method_text/>
        <rest_service/>
        <rest_service_text/>
        <rest_variables/>
        <role_conditions/>
        <script>(function executeRule(current, previous /*null when async*/) {
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Guard against the INSERT path. `previous` is null on insert, and a
    // brand-new case has no prior status, so there is no forward
    // transition to validate. Portal submissions insert with
    // status = Draft and must never be blocked here.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    if (!previous) {
        return;
    }

    var previousStatus = String(previous.status);
    var proposedStatus = String(current.status);

    // Only a genuine status change is a transition. Field-only updates
    // (subject, description, priority, assignment) are not this rule's
    // concern and are left to the other before-update rules.
    if (previousStatus === proposedStatus) {
        return;
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Map the proposed status onto the Flow Designer subflow that owns
    // its precondition. The subflow internal names are the natively
    // authored subflows in this scope; each one runs the shared
    // `Case Transition Guard` Custom Action, which delegates to
    // x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator so there is a single source of
    // truth for the transition rules and their verbatim messages.
    //
    // 'Draft' is deliberately absent: the Any -> Draft prohibition is
    // owned by x_casemgmt_block_draft_backtransition (order 200) and the
    // Closed -> * prohibition by x_casemgmt_block_terminal_closed
    // (order 100). Both run before this rule.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    var SUBFLOW_FOR_STATUS = {
        'Open': 'validate_open_transition',
        'In Progress': 'validate_in_progress_transition',
        'Pending': 'validate_pending_transition',
        'Resolved': 'validate_resolved_transition',
        'Closed': 'validate_closed_transition'
    };
    var subflowName = SUBFLOW_FOR_STATUS[proposedStatus];
    if (!subflowName) {
        return;
    }

    var caseSysId = String(current.getUniqueValue());

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // STEP 1 - run the Flow Designer subflow SYNCHRONOUSLY.
    //
    // Flow Designer record triggers (Created / Updated) fire AFTER the
    // database write commits, so a triggered flow can never abort a save
    // or surface a form-level blocking error. Invoking the subflow in the
    // foreground from this before-update rule is what makes the
    // state-machine flows load-bearing at the moment of the transition
    // instead of after it.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    var flowBlocked = null;
    try {
        var flowOutputs = sn_fd.FlowAPI.getRunner()
            .subflow('x_casemgmt.' + subflowName)
            .inForeground()
            .withInputs({ case_sys_id: caseSysId })
            .run()
            .getOutputs();
        flowBlocked = (String(flowOutputs['blocked']) === 'true');
    } catch (flowError) {
        // Fail closed onto the validator rather than silently allowing
        // the transition: STEP 2 below still decides the outcome.
        gs.warn('x_casemgmt_enforce_forward_transitions: subflow x_casemgmt.' + subflowName +
                ' could not be executed for case ' + caseSysId + ' - ' + flowError +
                '. Falling back to the in-flight CaseTransitionValidator evaluation.');
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // STEP 2 - evaluate the same gate against the IN-FLIGHT record.
    //
    // The subflow reads the case from the database, so it sees the
    // committed row. A single save may change `assigned_group` or
    // `assigned_agent` in the same transaction as `status`; in that case
    // the committed row is stale and only `current` reflects what will
    // actually be persisted. This step therefore decides the outcome,
    // using the identical x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator methods the
    // subflow's Custom Action calls, so both paths produce the same
    // verbatim messages. For a status-only save - which is what all six
    // UI Actions and the case form produce - the two verdicts are
    // identical and the subflow's verdict IS the decision.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    var validator = new x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator();
    var verdict;
    if (proposedStatus === 'Open') {
        verdict = validator.canTransitionToOpen(current);
    } else if (proposedStatus === 'In Progress') {
        verdict = validator.canTransitionToInProgress(current);
    } else if (proposedStatus === 'Resolved') {
        verdict = validator.canTransitionToResolved(current);
    } else if (proposedStatus === 'Closed') {
        verdict = validator.canTransitionToClosed(current, gs.getUserID());
    } else {
        // 'Pending' carries no precondition per the transition matrix.
        verdict = { ok: true };
    }

    // Record any divergence so an operator can see when a combined
    // field-and-status save made the committed row stale.
    if (flowBlocked !== null && flowBlocked !== !verdict.ok) {
        gs.info('x_casemgmt_enforce_forward_transitions: subflow x_casemgmt.' + subflowName +
                ' reported blocked=' + flowBlocked + ' while the in-flight evaluation reported blocked=' +
                (!verdict.ok) + ' for case ' + caseSysId + ' (' + previousStatus + ' -> ' + proposedStatus +
                '). The in-flight evaluation decides because it reflects the row as it will be saved.');
    }

    if (!verdict.ok) {
        // VERBATIM message from CaseTransitionValidator - do not paraphrase.
        gs.addErrorMessage(verdict.error);
        current.setAbortAction(true);
    }
})(current, previous);
</script>

sys_update_xml.name: Case Party Conditional Fields
sys_update_xml.payload:
true party_typeISNOTEMPTY^ORparty_typeISEMPTY^EQ Polymorphic field-rendering UI Policy on x_casemgmt_case_party. Implements the ServiceNow-native equivalent of ArkCase's @DiscriminatorColumn(cm_class_name) single-table inheritance pattern from PersonAssociation.java and the dual-table @ManyToOne pattern from PersonOrganizationAssociation.java per AAP Section 0.4.3 ("Polymorphic association via single-table choice + UI Policy"). Uses run_scripts=true with an imperative onCondition script to deterministically set field visibility and mandatory state for all three party_type values: "Person" (show person + mandatory; hide organization), "Organization" (show organization + mandatory; hide person), and empty (hide both fields, both not mandatory). The script_true block is the sole logic path; no declarative actions are used because the declarative two-policy approach with reverse_if_false=true has an unavoidable order-conflict in the empty-state case. Runs on form load (on_load=true) so existing case_party records render correctly when opened. The party_type field itself is mandatory at the dictionary level (../dictionary/x_casemgmt_case_party_party_type.xml), so users cannot save a record without picking one; the mandatory state of person/organization is therefore conditional on party_type and enforced ONLY through this UI Policy. true false Case Party Conditional Fields true 100 false true Polymorphic field rendering: show person+mandatory when party_type=Person, show organization+mandatory when party_type=Organization, hide both when party_type is empty. sys_ui_policy admin 2025-01-01 00:00:00 global 854295ebb4c8309eea6a52aa788ec8a9 0 x_casemgmt 82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af admin 2025-01-01 00:00:00 x_casemgmt_case_party

sys_update_xml.name: Open
sys_update_xml.payload:
x_casemgmt_case_open true false UI Action that transitions a Draft case to Open status. Visible only to x_casemgmt_case_manager users on cases with status=Draft. Delegates the assigned_group-populated check to x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator.canTransitionToOpen() (single source of truth shared with ../flows/sub_flows/validate_open_transition.xml). Per AAP Section 0.5.5 row 1 verbatim: "Draft -> Open: assigned_group populated - Surface form-level error". Server-side-only (no client prompt) - the transition has no required parameters beyond the assigned_group field that the operator should have populated on the form before clicking. Performs the transition on the server with defense-in-depth re-validation of role and status. Surfaces a form-level blocking error via gs.addErrorMessage if assigned_group is empty (verbatim message "Required field assigned_group is empty." returned by the Script Include). Contains zero gs.eventQueue() calls per the email-disabled constraint, zero hardcoded sys_id literals, and zero PII. true true false false false false primary false Open this case (assigned_group must be populated; case_manager role required). true false false false false false false false Open 100 x_casemgmt_case_manager false false false true sys_ui_action admin 2025-01-01 00:00:00 global / 2d897ab4b680731b3da534c9a667c658 0 x_casemgmt_case_open x_casemgmt 82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af sys_ui_action_x_casemgmt_case_open admin 2025-01-01 00:00:00 x_casemgmt_case

sys_update_xml.payload:
x_casemgmt_case_start_progress true false UI Action that transitions an Open case to In Progress status. Visible to x_casemgmt_case_manager (always) and x_casemgmt_case_agent (only when they are assigned to the case via assigned_agent or member of assigned_group, per AAP Section 0.5.6 Assigned-only rule). Server-side-only (no client prompt) - the transition has no required parameters beyond the assigned_agent and assigned_group fields that the operator should have populated on the form before clicking. Delegates the assigned_agent-populated AND member-of-assigned_group check to x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator.canTransitionToInProgress() (single source of truth shared with ../flows/sub_flows/validate_inprogress_transition.xml and ../business_rules/x_casemgmt_validate_assigned_agent_membership.xml). Per AAP Section 0.5.5 row 2 verbatim: "Open -> In Progress: assigned_agent populated AND member of assigned_group - Surface form-level error". Performs the transition on the server with defense-in-depth re-validation of role, status, and "Assigned only" assignment. Surfaces a form-level blocking error via gs.addErrorMessage if any guard fails (verbatim message returned by the Script Include). Contains zero gs.eventQueue() calls per the email-disabled constraint, zero hardcoded sys_id literals, and zero PII. true true false false false false primary false Start working on this case (assigned_agent must be populated and a member of assigned_group). true false false false false false false false Start Progress 200 x_casemgmt_case_manager,x_casemgmt_case_agent false false false true sys_ui_action admin 2025-01-01 00:00:00 global / e77dc24317a301765a60a3673ec7d164 0 x_casemgmt_case_start_progress x_casemgmt 82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af sys_ui_action_x_casemgmt_case_start_progress admin 2025-01-01 00:00:00 x_casemgmt_case

sys_update_xml.name: Set Pending
sys_update_xml.payload:
x_casemgmt_case_set_pending true true UI Action that transitions an In Progress case to Pending status. Visible to x_casemgmt_case_manager (always) and x_casemgmt_case_agent (only when assigned to the case via assigned_agent or member of assigned_group, per AAP Section 0.5.6 Assigned-only rule). Prompts the user for pending_reason (Awaiting Info / Awaiting Third Party / Other) on the client via a hybrid client+server pattern, then performs the transition on the server with defense-in-depth re-validation of role, status, assignment, and pending_reason. Per AAP Section 0.5.5 row 3 verbatim: "In Progress -> Pending: None; sets pending_reason (Awaiting Info / Awaiting Third Party / Other)". Companion to ../business_rules/x_casemgmt_clear_pending_reason_on_inprogress.xml which clears pending_reason on the reverse transition, and ../flows/sub_flows/validate_pending_transition.xml which handles the same transition at the Flow Designer workflow layer. Contains zero gs.eventQueue() calls per the email-disabled constraint, zero hardcoded sys_id literals, and zero PII. true true false false false false secondary false Pause this case (provide a pending reason). true false false false false false false false Set Pending onClickSetPending() 300 x_casemgmt_case_manager,x_casemgmt_case_agent false false false true sys_ui_action admin 2025-01-01 00:00:00 global / af34b659d531b7a994da7d1f6a5e09f1 0 x_casemgmt_case_set_pending x_casemgmt 82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af sys_ui_action_x_casemgmt_case_set_pending admin 2025-01-01 00:00:00 x_casemgmt_case

Contains zero gs.eventQueue() calls per the email-disabled constraint, zero hardcoded sys_id literals, and zero PII. true true false false false false primary false Resume work on this case (clears pending_reason). true false false false false false false false Resume 400 x_casemgmt_case_manager,x_casemgmt_case_agent false false false true sys_ui_action admin 2025-01-01 00:00:00 global / d48fd05fbca31c2194cac4b8645a2dbc 0 x_casemgmt_case_resume x_casemgmt 82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af sys_ui_action_x_casemgmt_case_resume admin 2025-01-01 00:00:00 x_casemgmt_case

sys_update_xml.payload:
x_casemgmt_case_resolve true false UI Action that transitions an In Progress case to Resolved status. Visible to x_casemgmt_case_manager (always) and x_casemgmt_case_agent (only when they are assigned to the case via assigned_agent or member of assigned_group, per AAP Section 0.5.6 Assigned-only rule). Delegates the all-tasks-closed check to x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator.canTransitionToResolved() (single source of truth shared with ../flows/sub_flows/validate_resolved_transition.xml). Per AAP Section 0.5.5 row 5 verbatim: "In Progress -> Resolved: All linked x_casemgmt_case_task records have status = Closed - Surface 'All tasks must be closed before resolving this case.'". Surfaces verbatim error message "All tasks must be closed before resolving this case." (per AAP Sections 0.5.5 and 0.7.4) when any child task has status != Closed. Server-side-only (no client prompt) - the transition has no required parameters beyond the existing child task rows on the case. Performs the transition on the server with defense-in-depth re-validation of role, status, and "Assigned only" assignment. Surfaces a form-level blocking error via gs.addErrorMessage if any guard fails (verbatim message returned by the Script Include). Contains zero gs.eventQueue() calls per the email-disabled constraint, zero hardcoded sys_id literals, and zero PII. true true false false false false primary false Resolve this case (all child tasks must be Closed). true false false false false false false false Resolve 500 x_casemgmt_case_manager,x_casemgmt_case_agent false false false true sys_ui_action admin 2025-01-01 00:00:00 global / fcef26b5dd69234a0b4a8ea82d997b17 0 x_casemgmt_case_resolve x_casemgmt 82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af sys_ui_action_x_casemgmt_case_resolve admin 2025-01-01 00:00:00 x_casemgmt_case

sys_update_xml.payload:
x_casemgmt_case_close true false UI Action that transitions a Resolved case to Closed status. Visible only to x_casemgmt_case_manager users on cases with status=Resolved (per AAP Section 0.5.5 row 6 verbatim: "Resolved -> Closed: Caller has x_casemgmt_case_manager role; auto-set closed_date - Surface form-level error"). Delegates the role check to x_casemgmt.CaseTransitionValidator.canTransitionToClosed() (single source of truth shared with ../flows/sub_flows/validate_closed_transition.xml). Server-side-only (no client prompt) - the transition has no required parameters beyond the existing Resolved status. Performs the transition on the server with defense-in-depth re-validation of role and status. Surfaces a form-level blocking error via gs.addErrorMessage if any guard fails (verbatim message "Only case managers can close cases." returned by the Script Include). The closed_date field is auto-populated by the cooperating ../business_rules/x_casemgmt_set_closed_date.xml before-update Business Rule (order=500) on the same current.update() transaction triggered by this UI Action - this UI Action sets only current.status='Closed', the BR sets current.closed_date=gs.nowDateTime(). After the transition completes, the ../business_rules/x_casemgmt_block_terminal_closed.xml before-update Business Rule (order=100) prevents any subsequent modifications to the case (per AAP Section 0.5.5 row 8 terminal-state rule). Contains zero gs.eventQueue() calls per the email-disabled constraint, zero hardcoded sys_id literals, and zero PII. true true false false false false destructive false Close this case (case_manager role required; case must be in Resolved status). closed_date will be auto-populated. This action is TERMINAL - the case cannot be modified after closure. true false false false false false false false Close 600 x_casemgmt_case_manager false false false true sys_ui_action admin 2025-01-01 00:00:00 global / c2988c82e1da1b3e1029196a6e0d0f9f 0 x_casemgmt_case_close x_casemgmt 82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af sys_ui_action_x_casemgmt_case_close admin 2025-01-01 00:00:00 x_casemgmt_case

sys_update_xml.name: Case Submission Widget
sys_update_xml.payload: custom body. Contains: * c.data.confirmationWidget - the embedded * confirmation widget instance loaded via * $sp.getWidget(). The success callback * mutates c.data.confirmationWidget.options. * number to pass the auto-generated case * number to the embedded widget. * c.data.submitted - boolean; flipped to * true after a successful POST. Drives * the conditional swap from the form panel * to the embedded confirmation widget panel. * c.data.submittedNumber - string; mirrors * the case number for any consumers that * want it directly off c.data (defense-in- * depth, in case the embedded widget's * options object is replaced rather than * mutated by some future refactor). * * Exposed method (template-bound): * c.submit() - executes the case submission. Issues * POST /api/x_casemgmt/case_submit with the * 5-field whitelisted payload via $http.post(). * On success (HTTP 201 with non-empty number), * sets c.data.submitted = true and mutates the * embedded confirmation widget's options.number * to the returned case number. On any error * (HTTP 4xx/5xx, network, missing number), * sets c.errorMessage to a generic, non-leaking * message so the verbatim alert is rendered. * * Design rationale: * - controller-as syntax (`var c = this`) per AAP Section 0.5.1's * widget-authoring conventions and per the sibling lookup widget * at ./sp_widget_x_casemgmt_case_lookup_widget.xml. * - $http (NOT fetch): Service Portal widgets run in AngularJS * 1.5.x context; $http is the canonical HTTP client. fetch() * would bypass AngularJS's digest cycle and require manual * $scope.$apply() handling. * - Strict 5-key payload (defense-in-depth): the POST body is * constructed by enumerating exactly the five whitelisted * fields, NOT by passing c.formData wholesale. Even if a future * refactor accidentally adds a sixth key to c.formData, the * POST body would still contain exactly the five whitelisted * fields. The server-side Script Include also drops any * non-whitelisted keys as a fallback, but the client-side * enumeration provides the first line of defense. * - Generic error message in template, NOT echoed from server: * the message "Submission failed. Please try again." is * hardcoded in this controller via direct assignment to * c.errorMessage. This controller deliberately does NOT pass * error.data.error or error.statusText to the template - the * server's error body is NEVER trusted by the client. This * matches the information-leakage hardening pattern used by * the sibling lookup widget. * - Identical handling of all HTTP errors: information-leakage * hardening. 400 (validation), 500 (server-error), 0 (network), * and "missing number on HTTP 200" all set the same generic * error. An attacker cannot distinguish "validation failed" * from "server error" from "network down" via the UX. * - c.submitting flag: prevents double-submit race conditions if * the user clicks the button twice quickly OR presses Enter * inside an input field while a request is in flight. The * ng-disabled binding on the button is the primary guard; * the early-return inside c.submit() is the defense-in-depth * fallback in case the disabled state is bypassed by a * keyboard event in an edge browser. * - String() coercion on response.data.number: ensures the * embedded widget's c.options.number is always a string, even * if the REST operation accidentally returns a number primitive. * Matches the embedded widget's own defensive coercion in * ./sp_widget_x_casemgmt_case_confirmation_widget.xml. */ var c = this; // Initialize the form state with empty values for each whitelisted field. // The whitelist (subject, type, description, requester_name, // requester_email) matches exactly the fields accepted by // /api/x_casemgmt/case_submit per AAP Section 0.4.4 and 0.7.4. c.formData = { subject: '', type: '', description: '', requester_name: '', requester_email: '' }; // Submission state flags. Initialized with safe defaults so the // template's ng-if and ng-disabled expressions evaluate cleanly // even before c.submit() runs. c.submitting = false; c.errorMessage = ''; /** * Submit the form data to the scripted REST endpoint at * POST /api/x_casemgmt/case_submit. * * Per AAP Section 0.4.4: posts EXACTLY the five whitelisted fields * (subject, type, description, requester_name, requester_email). * No additional fields are sent. * * Per AAP Section 0.4.4: on success, flips c.data.submitted to true * and passes the returned case number to the embedded confirmation * widget via c.data.confirmationWidget.options.number. The embedded * widget renders the verbatim message "Your case has been submitted" * plus the case number. * * Per AAP Section 0.7.2 (information-leakage hardening): on any * error (HTTP 4xx/5xx, network, missing number on HTTP 200), sets * c.errorMessage to the generic string "Submission failed. Please * try again." This function MUST NOT echo error.data.error, * error.statusText, or any server-supplied text. */ c.submit = function() { // Idempotent guard: prevent double-submit if the user clicks // the button or presses Enter while a request is in flight. // The button is also disabled in this case via ng-disabled, // but the guard provides defense-in-depth in case the disabled // state is bypassed by an edge browser's keyboard handling. if (c.submitting) { return; } // Reset state at the start of every submit. The error message // and submitting flag drive mutually-exclusive UI affordances. c.submitting = true; c.errorMessage = ''; // POST to the scripted REST endpoint. The payload is built by // enumerating EXACTLY the five whitelisted fields - NOT by // passing c.formData wholesale - so any future expansion of // c.formData does not accidentally widen the payload surface. // This is defense-in-depth alongside the server-side whitelist // enforced by x_casemgmt.CasePortalService.submitCase(). $http.post('/api/x_casemgmt/case_submit', { subject: c.formData.subject, type: c.formData.type, description: c.formData.description, requester_name: c.formData.requester_name, requester_email: c.formData.requester_email }).then(function(response) { // Success path (HTTP 2xx). The server's REST operation // returns { number, message } per its contract. c.submitting = false; if (response && response.data && response.data.number) { // Pass the returned case number to the embedded // confirmation widget by mutating its options.number. // The embedded widget's controller assigns // c.options = $scope.options; // so this mutation propagates reactively through // Angular's two-way binding. if (c.data.confirmationWidget && c.data.confirmationWidget.options) { c.data.confirmationWidget.options.number = String(response.data.number); } // Mirror the case number on c.data for any consumer that // wants it directly. Defense-in-depth in case the // embedded widget's options object is replaced rather // than mutated by some future refactor. c.data.submittedNumber = String(response.data.number); // Flip the submitted flag - the template swaps from // the form panel to the embedded confirmation widget. c.data.submitted = true; } else { // Defensive: HTTP 200 but no case number in the body. // This should never happen if the REST operation // conforms to its contract (it always returns either // { number, message } on success or { error } on // failure), but the guard prevents a confusing UX // where the form vanishes without a confirmation. c.errorMessage = 'Submission failed. Please try again.'; } }, function(error) { // Error path (HTTP 4xx, 5xx, or network failure / 0). // ALL error types are treated identically per the // information-leakage hardening discussed in the file // header comment. The generic error message is hardcoded // here in the controller; this function MUST NOT echo // error.data.error, error.statusText, or any server- // supplied content. c.submitting = false; c.errorMessage = 'Submission failed. Please try again.'; }); }; } ]]> c sp_instance Custom unauthenticated Service Portal widget for case submission. Renders a 5-field form (subject, type, description, requester_name, requester_email) and POSTs to /api/x_casemgmt/case_submit on Submit. On success, embeds the confirmation widget (sp_widget_x_casemgmt_case_confirmation_widget) via $sp.getWidget() and the <sp-widget> directive, passing the auto-generated case number through c.data.confirmationWidget.options.number so the embedded widget renders the verbatim message 'Your case has been submitted' plus the case number per AAP Section 0.4.4. On any HTTP error or missing-number response, displays a generic 'Submission failed. Please try again.' alert (no server diagnostics leaked). Embedded by sp_page_x_casemgmt_case_submit. The 5-field whitelist is enforced at three layers (form inputs, payload construction, and Script Include) for defense-in-depth. Replaces ArkCase's acm-service-portal-gateway DefaultPluggablePortalRequestService.submitRequest pattern. No client-side or server-side database operations - all writes flow through the scripted REST endpoint. Per AAP Sections 0.4.3, 0.4.4, 0.5.1, and 0.7.4 (verbatim 'Your case has been submitted' message lives in the embedded confirmation widget) and Validation Gate 4 (Portal - submission). false x_casemgmt_case_submission_widget false Case Submission Widget [] false true false sp_widget admin 2025-01-01 00:00:00 b40f252d17be5fa3b3bb85cb79ca8d2f 0 Case Submission Widget x_casemgmt 82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af sp_widget_x_casemgmt_case_submission_widget admin 2025-01-01 00:00:00

sys_update_xml.payload: custom * via $http.get(). On success (HTTP 200), sets * c.result with the strict 3-field whitelist. On * any error (HTTP 4xx/5xx, network), sets * c.notFound = true so the verbatim message is * rendered. * * Design rationale: * - controller-as syntax (`var c = this`) per AAP Section 0.5.1's * widget-authoring conventions and per the sibling confirmation * widget at ./sp_widget_x_casemgmt_case_confirmation_widget.xml. * - $http (NOT fetch): Service Portal widgets run in AngularJS * 1.5.x context; $http is the canonical HTTP client. fetch() * would bypass AngularJS's digest cycle and require manual * $scope.$apply() handling. * - encodeURIComponent on the case number: defensive URL escaping. * Even though normal case numbers (CASE0000001) contain no * special characters, defensive encoding prevents URL-injection * attacks if a malicious user submits a crafted string. * - Strict 3-field whitelist on response.data: defense-in-depth. * Even if the server's response somehow contained additional * fields (e.g., due to a future refactor of the Script Include), * this client controller extracts ONLY status/subject/opened_date * so no internal data leaks to the template. * - Verbatim error message in template, NOT echoed from server: * the message "No case found with that number." (AAP Section * 0.7.4) is hardcoded in the template via ng-if="c.notFound". * This controller deliberately does NOT pass error.data.error * or error.statusText to the template - the server's error * body is NEVER trusted by the client. * - Identical handling of all HTTP errors: information-leakage * hardening. 404 (not-found), 500 (server-error), 400 (bad- * request), and 0 (network-error) all set c.notFound = true. * An attacker cannot distinguish "case not found" from "API * down" from any other failure mode. * - c.loading flag: prevents double-lookup race conditions if * the user clicks the button twice quickly, AND drives the * "Looking up..." button text for clear UX feedback. */ var c = this; // Lookup state. Initialize with safe defaults so the template's // ng-if expressions evaluate cleanly even before c.lookup() runs. c.caseNumber = ''; c.result = null; c.notFound = false; c.loading = false; /** * Look up the status of a case by its number via the scripted REST * endpoint at /api/x_casemgmt/case_status_lookup. * * Per AAP Section 0.4.4: returns ONLY status, subject, opened_date * via strict 3-field whitelist on the response. * * Per AAP Section 0.7.4: on no-match (HTTP 404 or any other error), * the verbatim text "No case found with that number." is rendered * by the template. This function MUST NOT echo error.data.error or * any server-supplied text. */ c.lookup = function() { // Idempotent guard: prevent double-lookup if the user clicks // the button or presses Enter while a request is in flight. if (c.loading) { return; } // Empty-input guard: do not issue a request if the case number // is empty or whitespace-only. The button is also disabled in // this case via ng-disabled, but the guard provides defense- // in-depth in case the disabled state is bypassed (e.g., by // pressing Enter in some edge browsers). if (!c.caseNumber || String(c.caseNumber).trim() === '') { return; } // Reset state at the start of every lookup. The result panel // and the not-found panel are mutually exclusive: only one of // c.result and c.notFound can be truthy at any time. c.loading = true; c.result = null; c.notFound = false; // Build the URL with defensive URL-encoding of the case number. // The server-side Script Include x_casemgmt.CasePortalService. // lookupCase() trims whitespace and queries by the case 'number' // field. encodeURIComponent() handles any whitespace, special // characters, or potentially malicious input safely. var url = '/api/x_casemgmt/case_status_lookup?number=' + encodeURIComponent(String(c.caseNumber).trim()); $http.get(url).then(function(response) { // Success path (HTTP 200). The server's REST operation // returns { status, subject, opened_date } per its contract. c.loading = false; if (response && response.data) { // Strict 3-field whitelist (defense-in-depth). Extract // ONLY status, subject, opened_date from the response // body. Even if the server were misconfigured to return // additional fields, this widget would not display them. // String() coercion handles undefined/null gracefully - // the template renders an empty cell rather than the // literal text "undefined" or "null". c.result = { status: String(response.data.status || ''), subject: String(response.data.subject || ''), opened_date: String(response.data.opened_date || '') }; c.notFound = false; } else { // Defensive: empty response body but HTTP 200. Treat as // not-found rather than rendering an empty result panel. // This should not occur in practice (the server always // returns a body on 200) but guards against unexpected // upstream behavior. c.result = null; c.notFound = true; } }, function(error) { // Error path (HTTP 4xx, 5xx, or network failure / 0). // ALL error types are treated identically per the // information-leakage hardening discussed in the file // header comment. The verbatim text "No case found with // that number." (AAP Section 0.7.4) is rendered by the // template; this function MUST NOT echo error.data.error, // error.statusText, or any server-supplied content. c.loading = false; c.result = null; c.notFound = true; }); }; } ]]> c sp_instance Custom unauthenticated Service Portal widget for case status lookup. Renders a single case-number input field plus a Look Up Status button, GETs /api/x_casemgmt/case_status_lookup, and displays ONLY the whitelisted fields { status, subject, opened_date } on match or the verbatim text 'No case found with that number.' on no-match per AAP Section 0.7.4. Embedded by sp_page_x_casemgmt_case_status. No internal fields (assigned_group, assigned_agent, description, closed_date, requester_name, requester_email, priority, type, pending_reason, audit fields) are exposed. All HTTP errors (404, 500, 400, network) render the same verbatim message for information-leakage hardening. Replaces ArkCase's GetCaseByNumberServiceImpl.getCaseByNumber() and PortalRequestService.getRequestStatus() Spring services. No client-side or server-side database operations - all data flows through the scripted REST endpoint. Per AAP Sections 0.4.3, 0.4.4, 0.5.1, and 0.7.4 (verbatim no-case-found message) and Validation Gate 5 (Portal - lookup). false x_casemgmt_case_lookup_widget false Case Lookup Widget [] false true false sp_widget admin 2025-01-01 00:00:00 e992deb0bd1657f36a38f5af6a46aeb2 0 Case Lookup Widget x_casemgmt 82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af sp_widget_x_casemgmt_case_lookup_widget admin 2025-01-01 00:00:00

<record_update table="sys_ws_operation">
    <sys_ws_operation action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE">
        <active>true</active>
        <consumes/>
        <consumes_customized>false</consumes_customized>
        <default_operation_uri>/api/x_casemgmt/case_submit</default_operation_uri>
        <description>Anonymous POST handler for case submission.</description>
        <enforce_acl/>
        <http_method>POST</http_method>
        <name>Case Submit POST</name>
        <operation_script><![CDATA[(function process(/*RESTAPIRequest*/ request, /*RESTAPIResponse*/ response) {
    try {
        var body = request.body && request.body.data ? request.body.data : {};
        var portalSvc = new x_casemgmt.CasePortalService();
        var result = portalSvc.submitCase(body);
        response.setStatus(201);
        response.setBody({ result: result });
    } catch (e) {
        response.setStatus(400);
        response.setBody({ error: { message: (e && e.message) || 'Submission failed.' } });
    }
})(request, response);
]]></operation_script>

sys_update_xml.name: Case Status Lookup GET
sys_update_xml.payload:
<record_update table="sys_ws_operation">
    <sys_ws_operation action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE">
        <active>true</active>
        <consumes/>
        <consumes_customized>false</consumes_customized>
        <default_operation_uri>/api/x_casemgmt/case_status_lookup</default_operation_uri>
        <description>Anonymous GET handler for case status lookup. Returns the verbatim string No case found with that number. on no-match per AAP Section 0.7.4.</description>
        <enforce_acl/>
        <http_method>GET</http_method>
        <name>Case Status Lookup GET</name>
        <operation_script><![CDATA[(function process(/*RESTAPIRequest*/ request, /*RESTAPIResponse*/ response) {
    try {
        var caseNumber = request.queryParams && request.queryParams.number ? String(request.queryParams.number) : '';
        var portalSvc = new x_casemgmt.CasePortalService();
        var result = portalSvc.lookupCase(caseNumber);
        if (result && result.error) {
            // Verbatim message per AAP Section 0.7.4: No case found with that number.
            response.setStatus(404);
            response.setBody({ result: { error: 'No case found with that number.' } });
            return;
        }
        response.setStatus(200);
        response.setBody({ result: result });
    } catch (e) {
        response.setStatus(500);
        response.setBody({ error: { message: 'Internal lookup error.' } });
    }
})(request, response);
]]></operation_script>
        <operation_uri>/api/x_casemgmt/case_status_lookup</operation_uri>
        <produces/>
        <produces_customized>false</produces_customized>
        <relative_path>/</relative_path>

        <short_description>Anonymous GET handler for case status lookup. Returns the verbatim string No case found with that number. on no-match per AAP Section 0.7.4.</short_description>

Replaces ArkCase's CaseFile.caseType + Pentaho aggregation pipeline with a native GlideAggregate-backed sys_report. Different aggregation than x_casemgmt_all_cases_by_status (group by status) and x_casemgmt_all_cases_by_priority (group by priority); same dashboard audience per AAP Section 0.4.4. type false false x_casemgmt_all_cases_by_type sys_report admin 2025-01-01 00:00:00 f35f0a22b19d6e5385538eb3febb1a84 0 All Cases by Type x_casemgmt 82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af sys_report_x_casemgmt_all_cases_by_type admin 2025-01-01 00:00:00 x_casemgmt_case
All Cases by Type pie

sys_update_xml.name: x_casemgmt_all_cases_by_priority
sys_update_xml.payload:
COUNT medium Manager View dashboard bar widget data source. Aggregates ALL records in x_casemgmt_case grouped by the priority Choice field with COUNT(*) per bucket. Four bars expected (Low, Medium, High, Critical) when seed data spans all priority tiers. UNFILTERED by design - shows the entire team backlog distribution across the urgency tiers including terminal-state cases, enabling managers to assess whether the team is over-indexed on Critical/High volume (signals operational stress) or whether Low/Medium cases dominate (signals normal intake mix). Replaces ArkCase's CaseFile.priority + Pentaho aggregation pipeline with a native GlideAggregate-backed sys_report. Different aggregation than x_casemgmt_all_cases_by_status (group by status) and x_casemgmt_all_cases_by_type (group by type); same Manager View dashboard audience per AAP Section 0.4.4. Same chart type as x_casemgmt_all_cases_by_status (bar) but lower-cardinality grouping (4 ordinal urgency tiers vs. 6 lifecycle stages); ordinal urgency tiers benefit from left-to-right linear ordering inherent to bar charts. priority false false x_casemgmt_all_cases_by_priority sys_report admin 2025-01-01 00:00:00 f4c76c4c0bb1643542ac6347ddf9edcd 0 All Cases by Priority x_casemgmt 82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af sys_report_x_casemgmt_all_cases_by_priority admin 2025-01-01 00:00:00 x_casemgmt_case
All Cases by Priority bar

sys_update_xml.name: x_casemgmt_avg_time_to_close
sys_update_xml.payload:
AVG duration_to_close medium Manager View dashboard single-score widget for AVG(closed_date - opened_date) over x_casemgmt_case records at status=Closed. The aggregation source `duration_to_close` is a Function Field defined in ../dictionary/x_casemgmt_case_duration_to_close.xml whose value is computed at query time by the platform's database-level function `glidefunction:datediff(closed_date,opened_date)`. The widget renders a Duration AVG (e.g., "5 Days 03:42:11") of elapsed time between case opening and closure. Filter excludes non-Closed cases whose closed_date is NULL by definition. No external BI engine; uses native GlideAggregate. Satisfies AAP Section 0.7.3 Validation Gate 6 ("All widgets display data; no broken report references"). status=Closed false false x_casemgmt_avg_time_to_close sys_report admin 2025-01-01 00:00:00 79fabb5f5754b629205b2382face3ebb 0 Average Time to Close x_casemgmt 82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af sys_report_x_casemgmt_avg_time_to_close admin 2025-01-01 00:00:00 x_casemgmt_case
Average Time to Close single_score

sys_update_xml.name: x_casemgmt_cases_opened_30d
sys_update_xml.payload:
COUNT medium Manager View dashboard single-score widget computing COUNT(*) over x_casemgmt_case records whose opened_date falls within the trailing 30-day window. The 30-day cutoff is resolved at query-execution time via javascript:gs.daysAgoStart(30), which returns midnight of the day exactly 30 days before "now" in the system timezone - a rolling window stable across calendar time and portable across PDIs. Single scalar result, on-demand evaluation. No external BI engine; uses native GlideAggregate. Replaces ArkCase's Pentaho/Solr time-bucketed CaseSummaryByStatusAndTimePeriodDto aggregate pattern with a native single_score sys_report. opened_date>=javascript:gs.daysAgoStart(30) false false x_casemgmt_cases_opened_30d sys_report admin 2025-01-01 00:00:00 95b2127b026a92ba5e041a8d4d7277ec 0 Cases Opened in Last 30 Days x_casemgmt 82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af sys_report_x_casemgmt_cases_opened_30d admin 2025-01-01 00:00:00 x_casemgmt_case

Renders the ../reports/x_casemgmt_my_open_cases.xml report (type=list) showing the cases assigned to the current user where status NOT IN (Resolved, Closed). Per the underlying report's filter, this is "the agent's daily-driver list" - the rows the agent will work on today.
Position math (12-column grid): column=1, width=6 -> occupies columns 1-6 row=1, height=4 -> occupies rows 1-4
Per AAP Section 0.4.4, this is the "MY work-in-flight" view that an agent reaches for FIRST when opening their dashboard. Top-left is the natural eye-scan starting point on any LTR-language dashboard. Per Validation Gate 6, this widget MUST render with at least 1 row from x_casemgmt_case where assigned_agent = the demo agent's sys_id AND status NOT IN (Resolved, Closed). Per AAP Section 0.4.1, demo cases 02, 03, 04, 07, 08 are in {Open, In Progress, Pending} statuses; the demo agent MUST be assigned_agent on at least one of these (the seed-data agent ensures this).
Why a list widget (not a chart): per AAP Section 0.4.4, the agent needs ROW-LEVEL detail to click into individual cases. A donut/bar would obscure case-level access. The list widget renders each row clickable, navigating to the case form on click - matching ArkCase's "case list -> case detail" UX flow.

Renders the ../reports/x_casemgmt_my_overdue_tasks.xml report (type=list) showing the tasks assigned to the current user where due_date < today AND status != Closed. Per the underlying report's filter, this is "the agent's overdue work" - tasks that have slipped past their deadline and need immediate action.
Position math (12-column grid): column=7, width=6 -> occupies columns 7-12 row=1, height=4 -> occupies rows 1-4
Per AAP Section 0.4.4, this is the "fire-fighting view" that an agent reaches for SECOND. Whereas Widget 1 shows all assigned cases regardless of urgency, Widget 2 surfaces tasks (which are more granular than cases) that are explicitly overdue. The overdue-tasks list directly drives the prioritization decision: which task to work on RIGHT NOW. Per Validation Gate 6, this widget MUST render with at least 1 row from x_casemgmt_case_task where assigned_to = demo agent AND due_date < today AND status != Closed (the seed-data agent ensures this by setting at least one demo task with a past due_date).
Why a list widget (not a chart): same reasoning as Widget 1 - the agent needs ROW-LEVEL detail to click into individual tasks and update their status. A chart would obscure task-level access.
Cross-references: - <dashboard>: record [2] in this file. - <tab>: record [3] in this file. - <report>: ../reports/x_casemgmt_my_overdue_tasks.xml (verified to have <name>x_casemgmt_my_overdue_tasks</name> and <title>My Overdue Tasks</title>). --> <pa_dashboard_widgets action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"> <column>7</column> <dashboard display_value="Agent Workspace">x_casemgmt_agent_workspace</dashboard> <height>4</height> <name>x_casemgmt_agent_workspace_widget_my_overdue_tasks</name> <order>20</order> <report display_value="My Overdue Tasks">x_casemgmt_my_overdue_tasks</report> <row>1</row> <sys_class_name>pa_dashboard_widgets</sys_class_name> <sys_created_by>admin</sys_created_by> <sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on> <sys_id>6c5338b94cdba04e62914586f4e12057</sys_id> <sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count> <sys_name>My Overdue Tasks</sys_name> <sys_package display_value="Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">x_casemgmt</sys_package> <sys_policy/> <sys_scope display_value="Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope> <sys_update_name>pa_dashboard_widgets_x_casemgmt_agent_workspace_widget_my_overdue_tasks</sys_update_name> <sys_updated_by>admin</sys_updated_by> <sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on> <tab display_value="Overview">x_casemgmt_agent_workspace_tab_main</tab> <title>My Overdue Tasks</title> <type>report</type> <width>6</width> </pa_dashboard_widgets>
<!-- =================================================================== RECORD [7] - WIDGET 3: CASE COUNT BY STATUS (DONUT/PIE CHART) =================================================================== The full-width donut chart on row 2. Renders the ../reports/x_casemgmt_case_count_by_status.xml report (type=pie) showing the count of all cases (across the entire team, not just the current agent) grouped by status. The six slices correspond to the six values of x_casemgmt_case.status: Draft, Open, In Progress, Pending, Resolved, Closed.
Position math (12-column grid): column=1, width=12 -> occupies columns 1-12 (full row) row=5, height=4 -> occupies rows 5-8
Per AAP Section 0.4.4, this is the "team-wide context" view that gives the agent perspective on how their work fits into the broader case distribution. While Widgets 1 and 2 are PERSONAL (filter by current user), Widget 3 is GLOBAL (no current-user filter). It deliberately spans the full width of the row because donut chart legibility benefits from horizontal space for slice labels and a horizontal legend.
Why a donut chart (not a bar): per AAP Section 0.4.4, the deliberate diversity of chart types pairs different chart types to different cardinalities - donut is suitable for low-to-medium cardinality (6 buckets here) where the focus is PROPORTIONS. The agent typically wants to see "what fraction of cases are Open vs Closed vs In Progress" rather than absolute counts. Bar would be appropriate for ordered comparison (e.g., priority); donut is appropriate for unordered proportional comparison.
Per Validation Gate 6, this widget MUST render with all six slices populated since AAP Section 0.4.1 mandates seed data spanning all six status values (demo cases 01-10 hit Draft, Open, In Progress, Pending, Resolved, Closed - one or more per status).
Cross-references: - <dashboard>: record [2] in this file. - <tab>: record [3] in this file. - <report>: ../reports/x_casemgmt_case_count_by_status.xml (verified to have <name>x_casemgmt_case_count_by_status</name> and <title>Case Count by Status</title>). --> <pa_dashboard_widgets action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"> <column>1</column> <dashboard display_value="Agent Workspace">x_casemgmt_agent_workspace</dashboard> <height>4</height> <name>x_casemgmt_agent_workspace_widget_case_count_by_status</name> <order>30</order> <report display_value="Case Count by Status">x_casemgmt_case_count_by_status</report> <row>5</row> <sys_class_name>pa_dashboard_widgets</sys_class_name> <sys_created_by>admin</sys_created_by> <sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on> <sys_id>4920c9d42b6499f2fe6b1c833cbda375</sys_id> <sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count> <sys_name>Case Count by Status</sys_name> <sys_package display_value="Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">x_casemgmt</sys_package> <sys_policy/> <sys_scope display_value="Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope> <sys_update_name>pa_dashboard_widgets_x_casemgmt_agent_workspace_widget_case_count_by_status</sys_update_name> <sys_updated_by>admin</sys_updated_by> <sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on> <tab display_value="Overview">x_casemgmt_agent_workspace_tab_main</tab> <title>Case Count by Status</title> <type>report</type> <width>12</width> </pa_dashboard_widgets>
<!-- =================================================================== RECORD [8] - ROLE ATTACHMENT (pa_dashboard_role) - case_agent =================================================================== Binds this dashboard to the x_casemgmt_case_agent scoped role. Per the assigned-folder requirements ("Agent Workspace dashboard MUST be visible to x_casemgmt_case_agent (operationally relevant)"), this is the FIRST of two role attachments for this dashboard.
Visibility outcome (combined with record [9]): - Users WITH x_casemgmt_case_agent role: Dashboard appears in the Performance Analytics dashboard catalog and renders all three widgets. Widget 1 shows cases assigned to this user; Widget 2 shows tasks assigned to this user; Widget 3 shows team-wide status distribution. - Users WITH x_casemgmt_case_manager role (record [9]): Dashboard appears in the catalog. Widgets 1 and 2 may render empty if the manager has no personally-assigned cases or tasks; Widget 3 renders fully (team-wide). Managers use this dashboard primarily to monitor agents, with their detailed KPIs in the Manager View dashboard. - Users WITHOUT either role (including x_casemgmt_case_viewer): Dashboard does NOT appear in the catalog by default. Per the assigned-folder requirements, viewers can be "explicitly granted" access on a per-deployment basis - that's a future enhancement, not part of this POC. - Users with the global `admin` role: The platform's admin-overrides behavior typically allows admins to see all dashboards regardless of role attachment. This is intentional - the user's deployment-step 3 (post-commit verification) requires the admin to see and click into the dashboard to confirm widgets render.
Per AAP Section 0.7.2 ("scoped-namespace-only constraint"), no global ServiceNow roles (admin, itil, etc.) are attached here.
Cross-references: - <dashboard>: record [2] in this file (x_casemgmt_agent_workspace). - <role>: ../roles/sys_user_role_x_casemgmt_case_agent.xml (verified to have <name>x_casemgmt_case_agent</name>).
This record has no <name> field; sys_update_name carries the canonical identifier for the Update-Set engine. --> <pa_dashboard_role action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"> <dashboard display_value="Agent Workspace">x_casemgmt_agent_workspace</dashboard> <role display_value="x_casemgmt_case_agent">x_casemgmt_case_agent</role> <sys_class_name>pa_dashboard_role</sys_class_name> <sys_created_by>admin</sys_created_by> <sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on> <sys_id>bcf719869145ede8d31c6c6899c8df20</sys_id> <sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count> <sys_package display_value="Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">x_casemgmt</sys_package> <sys_policy/> <sys_scope display_value="Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope> <sys_update_name>pa_dashboard_role_x_casemgmt_agent_workspace_case_agent</sys_update_name> <sys_updated_by>admin</sys_updated_by> <sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on> </pa_dashboard_role>
<!-- =================================================================== RECORD [9] - ROLE ATTACHMENT (pa_dashboard_role) - case_manager =================================================================== Binds this dashboard to the x_casemgmt_case_manager scoped role. Per the assigned-folder requirements ("Agent Workspace dashboard MUST be visible ... AND to x_casemgmt_case_manager (monitoring agents)"), this is the SECOND of two role attachments for this dashboard.
Why managers also get the agent dashboard: Managers oversee agents and need access to the same operational view that agents see. The Manager View dashboard (../dashboards/pa_dashboards_x_casemgmt_manager_view.xml) shows team-wide KPIs (status/type/priority distributions, average time-to-close, intake volume), but it does NOT show "MY open cases" or "MY overdue tasks" because a manager rarely has personally-assigned cases. By granting managers access to BOTH dashboards, they can: - Use the Manager View to monitor team-wide health. - Use this Agent Workspace to spot-check the same operational view that agents see, e.g., to validate Widget 3's status distribution matches the Manager View's bar chart. - On the rare occasion they DO have a personally-assigned case (e.g., they are an escalation owner), see it in Widget 1.
Cross-references: - <dashboard>: record [2] in this file (x_casemgmt_agent_workspace). - <role>: ../roles/sys_user_role_x_casemgmt_case_manager.xml (verified to have <name>x_casemgmt_case_manager</name>).
This record has no <name> field; sys_update_name carries the canonical identifier for the Update-Set engine. --> <pa_dashboard_role action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"> <dashboard display_value="Agent Workspace">x_casemgmt_agent_workspace</dashboard> <role display_value="x_casemgmt_case_manager">x_casemgmt_case_manager</role> <sys_class_name>pa_dashboard_role</sys_class_name> <sys_created_by>admin</sys_created_by> <sys_created_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_created_on> <sys_id>2cf576608fe7cdfeac60cb73381b3355</sys_id> <sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count> <sys_package display_value="Case Management" source="x_casemgmt">x_casemgmt</sys_package> <sys_policy/> <sys_scope display_value="Case Management">82b99028936f74320d74d6f88357a5af</sys_scope> <sys_update_name>pa_dashboard_role_x_casemgmt_agent_workspace_case_manager</sys_update_name> <sys_updated_by>admin</sys_updated_by> <sys_updated_on>2025-01-01 00:00:00</sys_updated_on> </pa_dashboard_role> </unload>
